title.en: Volume 434 Biographies 221: Shen Dihui, Deng Renkun, Yu Bingdao, Li Yao, Zhu Sunyi, Shi Zhie, Liu Huangao, Zhu Shan Zhang Zi Zhi Zhen, Huang Fu Chen Zi Peng Nian
title.raw: 卷434 列傳二百二十一 沈棣辉 邓仁堃 余炳焘 栗燿 朱孙贻 史致谔 刘郇膏 朱善张子之榛 黄辅辰子彭年

sentences.zh: 列傳二百二十一

translations.literal: Biographies 221
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 221

sentences.zh: 沈棣輝鄧仁堃余炳燾栗燿硃孫貽史致諤

translations.literal: Shen Dihui, Deng Renkun, Yu Bingtao, Li Yao, Zhu Sunyi, Shi Zhie
translations.idiomatic: Shen Dihui, Deng Renkun, Yu Bingtao, Li Yao, Zhu Sunyi, and Shi Zhie

sentences.zh: 劉郇膏硃善張子之榛黃輔辰子彭年

translations.literal: Liu Huangao, Zhu Shan, Zhang Zizhen, Huang Fuchen, Zi Pengnian
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huangao, Zhu Shan, Zhang Zizhen, Huang Fuchen, and Zi Pengnian

sentences.zh: 沈棣輝，字奏篪，浙江歸安人。

translations.literal: Shen Dihui, style name Zouci, was a native of Gui'an in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Dihui, whose style was Zouci, came from Gui'an in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 少游淮上，為河督麟慶司章奏。

translations.literal: In his youth he traveled on the Huai region and served Grand Canal Director Lin Qing as secretary for memorials.
translations.idiomatic: While still young he traveled along the Huai, serving Grand Canal Director Lin Qing as his memorial secretary.

sentences.zh: 道光中，納貲為廣東通判，補廣州永寧通判。

translations.literal: During the Daoguang reign he purchased office and became sub-prefect of Guangdong, appointed sub-prefect of Yongning in Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daoguang era he bought his way into office as a Guangdong sub-prefect and was posted to Yongning in the Guangzhou prefecture.

sentences.zh: 擢黃岡同知，以功晉知府，補韶州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to sub-prefect of Huanggang, then advanced to prefect for merit and assigned to Shaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to sub-prefect of Huanggang, he was later raised to prefect for his achievements and appointed to Shaozhou.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，調署廉州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he was transferred to act as prefect of Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng he was transferred to serve as acting prefect of Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 時嶺嶠群盜並起，李士奎、顏品瑤、黃春晚等分踞欽州之那彭，靈山之林墟，眾數十萬。

translations.literal: At that time bandits rose throughout the Lingnan ridges; Li Shikui, Yan Pinyao, Huang Chunwan and others seized Napeng in Qinzhou and Linxu in Lingshan, their forces numbering hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were rising everywhere across the Lingnan passes; Li Shikui, Yan Pinyao, Huang Chunwan, and others held Napeng in Qinzhou and Linxu in Lingshan, with forces said to number in the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 棣輝至，出賊不意，率兵二千掩入那彭，殲之。

translations.literal: When Dihui arrived he took the rebels by surprise, led two thousand troops in a raid on Napeng, and annihilated them.
translations.idiomatic: When Dihui arrived he caught the rebels off guard, led two thousand men in a surprise strike on Napeng, and wiped them out.

sentences.zh: 急分千人趨林墟，賊空壁出關，棣輝已由間道入其巢，遂連克旁近諸賊壘。

translations.literal: He urgently detached a thousand men to rush to Linxu; the rebels emptied their fort to sally out, while Dihui had already entered their nest by a side path, and thus captured in succession the nearby rebel strongholds.
translations.idiomatic: He quickly sent a thousand men toward Linxu; the rebels marched out with their walls bare, while Dihui had already slipped in by a hidden route and took one neighboring rebel fort after another.

sentences.zh: 博白賊劉八伺隙襲廉州，馳還，遇賊五里亭，令列陣以待。

translations.literal: The Bobai rebel Liu Ba seized the chance to attack Lianzhou; Dihui galloped back and met the rebels at Wuliting, ordering his troops to form battle lines and wait.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ba of Bobai seized an opening to strike Lianzhou; Dihui raced back, met the rebels at Wuliting, and ordered his men to form up and hold their ground.

sentences.zh: 賊疑有伏，稍引去，呼噪乘之，賊大潰。

translations.literal: The rebels suspected an ambush and withdrew slightly; he shouted and charged them, and the rebels broke in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels suspected an ambush and drew back a little; he raised a shout and pressed the attack, and they broke and fled in disorder.

sentences.zh: 休兵十日而進，又殲賊靈山早禾湧，追至廣西橫州，斬劉八。

translations.literal: After ten days' rest he advanced again, destroyed the rebels at Lingshan's Zaoheyu, pursued them to Hengzhou in Guangxi, and beheaded Liu Ba.
translations.idiomatic: After ten days' rest he advanced again, wiped out the rebels at Lingshan's Zaoheyu, pursued them to Hengzhou in Guangxi, and beheaded Liu Ba.

sentences.zh: 廉州平。

translations.literal: Lianzhou was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Lianzhou was pacified.

sentences.zh: 總督徐廣縉駐梧州，剿艇匪，檄棣輝出鬱林，援潯州。

translations.literal: Governor-General Xu Guangjin was stationed at Wuzhou suppressing boat bandits and ordered Dihui out from Yulin to relieve Xunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Governor-General Xu Guangjin was at Wuzhou suppressing boat bandits and ordered Dihui out from Yulin to relieve Xunzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊舟數百圍城，攻甚急。

translations.literal: Several hundred rebel boats besieged the city and attacked fiercely.
translations.idiomatic: Several hundred rebel boats besieged the city and pressed the assault hard.

sentences.zh: 遣卒梯而入，約期會戰，伏兵兩岸，縱火焚賊舟，與城兵夾擊，大破之。

translations.literal: He sent men up ladders into the city to arrange a coordinated battle date, placed ambushes on both banks, set fires to burn the rebel boats, and with city troops attacked from both sides, inflicting a great defeat.
translations.idiomatic: He sent men in over ladders to fix a day for a joint attack, hid troops on both banks, set fire to the rebel boats, and with the garrison struck from both sides, winning a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 督諸軍窮追，梧州水師邀擊，沉賊舟無脫者。

translations.literal: He urged all armies in hot pursuit; the Wuzhou naval force intercepted and sank the rebel boats without any escaping.
translations.idiomatic: He drove every unit in relentless pursuit; the Wuzhou naval force intercepted them and sank the rebel boats until none escaped.

sentences.zh: 論功，加按察使銜。

translations.literal: For his merit he was given the rank of surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was given the rank of surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時廣西賊竄湖南，徐廣縉督師移剿，棣輝隨參軍事。

translations.literal: At the time Guangxi rebels fled into Hunan; Xu Guangjin moved his headquarters to pursue them, and Dihui accompanied him on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Guangxi rebels were then fleeing into Hunan; Xu Guangjin shifted his command to pursue them, and Dihui went with him as a military adviser.

sentences.zh: 廣縉罷，葉名琛督兩廣，調棣輝回廣東治軍需。

translations.literal: When Guangjin was dismissed, Ye Mingchen became governor-general of the two Guang; Dihui was recalled to Guangdong to manage military supplies.
translations.idiomatic: After Guangjin was removed, Ye Mingchen took charge of the two Guang provinces and recalled Dihui to Guangdong to handle military logistics.

sentences.zh: 先已授廣西左江道，至是調肇羅道。

translations.literal: He had already been appointed Left River Circuit intendant of Guangxi; now he was transferred to Zhao-Luo Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He had already been made intendant of Guangxi's Left River Circuit; he was now transferred to the Zhao-Luo Circuit.

sentences.zh: 四年，署廣東鹽運使。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he acted as Guangdong salt transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he served as acting Guangdong salt transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 陳開者，廣州匪首，倡亂踞佛山。

translations.literal: Chen Kai was a bandit chieftain of Guangzhou who raised rebellion and seized Foshan.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Kai was a Guangzhou bandit leader who raised a revolt and seized Foshan.

sentences.zh: 群賊何子海、豆皮春、李文茂等應之，踞石門金官窯為犄角。

translations.literal: The bandits He Zihai, Doupichun, Li Wenmao and others responded, holding the Jinguanyao at Shimen as a flank position.
translations.idiomatic: He Zihai, Doupichun, Li Wenmao, and other chiefs joined him, holding the Jinguanyao at Shimen as a supporting strongpoint.

sentences.zh: 連陷數十州縣，環省皆賊壘。

translations.literal: They captured successively dozens of prefectures and counties; rebel forts ringed the province.
translations.idiomatic: They took one prefecture and county after another until rebel camps ringed the province.

sentences.zh: 賊渠陳光龍屯河南岸，何博奮海艇千餘踞省河，道路梗塞，外援皆絕。

translations.literal: The rebel leader Chen Guanglong camped on the south bank of the river; He Bo seized more than a thousand warships on the provincial river; roads were blocked and outside aid was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel chief Chen Guanglong held the south bank; He Bo with more than a thousand war junks dominated the provincial river; roads were cut and outside relief was severed.

sentences.zh: 名琛悉以軍事付棣輝。

translations.literal: Mingchen entrusted all military affairs to Dihui.
translations.idiomatic: Mingchen placed all military affairs in Dihui's hands.

sentences.zh: 選精銳四千人，以二千駐流橋、西山廟，為兩翼；

translations.literal: He selected four thousand crack troops, stationing two thousand at Liuqiao and Xishan Temple as the two wings;
translations.idiomatic: He picked four thousand elite troops, posting two thousand at Liuqiao and Xishan Temple as his two wings;

sentences.zh: 以千人伏城中，出小西門分佈要害，多張旗幟為疑兵。

translations.literal: a thousand were hidden in the city; they went out the Lesser West Gate and spread through key points, setting up many banners as decoy troops.
translations.idiomatic: another thousand lay hidden in the city, sallied from the Lesser West Gate to hold key points, and raised many banners as a feint.

sentences.zh: 賊四面薄城，城內發砲中賊，陣亂，縱兵擊之，斬級千，賊自是不敢近​​城。

translations.literal: Rebels pressed the city from four sides; the city fired cannon and hit the rebels; their formation broke; he loosed his troops and struck, beheading more than a thousand; the rebels from then dared not approach the city.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pressed in from all four sides; the garrison fired cannon into their ranks and broke their formation; he unleashed his troops and cut down more than a thousand heads, after which the rebels no longer dared approach the walls.

sentences.zh: 至十一月，圍未解。

translations.literal: By the eleventh month the siege had not been lifted.
translations.idiomatic: By the eleventh month the siege still had not been broken.

sentences.zh: 棣輝謀於眾曰：「今外無援兵，內無積儲。

translations.literal: Dihui consulted the assembly, saying: "Now there is no relief army outside and no stores within.
translations.idiomatic: Dihui laid the situation before his officers: "We have no relief from outside and no reserves within.

sentences.zh: 聞賊中因爭食內攜，急擊不可失！」

translations.literal: I hear the rebels quarrel over food and turn on one another; we must strike quickly and not miss the chance!"
translations.idiomatic: I hear the rebels are quarreling over food and falling out among themselves—we must strike at once and not let the chance slip!"

sentences.zh: 乃自將千人出攻小港橋賊壘。

translations.literal: Thereupon he personally led a thousand men to attack the rebel fort at Xiaogang Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: He then led a thousand men himself against the rebel fort at Xiaogang Bridge.

sentences.zh: 日晡未下，忽見賊營火起，大呼曰：「賊破矣！」

translations.literal: By dusk it had not fallen; suddenly fires rose in the rebel camp; he shouted loudly: "The rebels are broken!"
translations.idiomatic: By late afternoon the fort still stood; then flames burst up in the rebel camp and he shouted, "The rebels are broken!"

sentences.zh: 士卒皆奮，克之。

translations.literal: The soldiers all took heart and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: His men took heart and carried it.

sentences.zh: 乘勝進攻佛山，值大霧，賊不虞其至，連戰皆捷，遂復佛山。

translations.literal: Pressing victory he advanced on Foshan; a heavy fog fell; the rebels did not expect his arrival; battle after battle he won; Foshan was recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Riding the momentum he pushed on to Foshan; a thick fog rolled in and the rebels did not expect him; battle after battle went his way, and Foshan was retaken.

sentences.zh: 聞東莞水賊由石門犯省城，還軍救之。

translations.literal: Hearing that Dongguan water bandits were entering the provincial capital by Shimen, he turned his army to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Dongguan water bandits were moving on the provincial capital through Shimen, he turned his army back to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 至黃竹岐，賊船數千，官軍僅數百艘，又居下風，勢甚危。

translations.literal: At Huangzhuqi rebel boats numbered thousands while government boats were only hundreds, and moreover they were to leeward—the situation was very dangerous.
translations.idiomatic: At Huangzhuqi the rebels had thousands of boats while the government fleet numbered only in the hundreds and lay to leeward—the odds were desperate.

sentences.zh: 棣輝禱於南海神，俄而反風，令裨將何高漢駕艨艟衝入賊陣，碎其乘舟，大破之，殺賊萬餘，俘數千，溺死者無算。

translations.literal: Dihui prayed to the Nanhai god; soon the wind reversed; he ordered Lieutenant He Gaohan to drive a tower ship into the rebel formation, smashing their boats, inflicting a great defeat, killing more than ten thousand rebels, capturing thousands, with countless drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Dihui prayed to the god of the Southern Sea; soon the wind shifted; he sent Lieutenant He Gaohan in a tower ship straight into the rebel line, smashing their vessels and winning a crushing victory—more than ten thousand rebels killed, thousands taken, and untold numbers drowned.

sentences.zh: 危城獲全，又分兵殲賊酋黃福於潭州。

translations.literal: The perilous city was preserved; he also detached troops and destroyed the rebel chieftain Huang Fu at Tanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The endangered city was saved; he also detached a force and destroyed the rebel chief Huang Fu at Tanzhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，复順德、清遠、英德。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Shunde, Qingyuan and Yingde were recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Shunde, Qingyuan, and Yingde were recovered.

sentences.zh: 賊圍韶州城已年餘，至是聞援兵至，遁。

translations.literal: Rebels had besieged Shaozhou city for more than a year; on hearing relief troops had come they fled.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels had besieged Shaozhou for more than a year; when they heard relief was coming they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 南北路悉平，擢按察使。

translations.literal: North and south routes were all pacified; he was promoted surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The northern and southern routes were fully pacified, and he was promoted to surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 六年，擢貴州布政使，未之任，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was promoted to Guizhou administration commissioner but did not take up the post before he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was promoted to administration commissioner of Guizhou but died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 賜卹，贈內閣學士。

translations.literal: Condolence gifts were granted and he was posthumously given Grand Secretariat bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: Condolence gifts were granted and he was posthumously made a Grand Secretariat bachelor.

sentences.zh: 棣輝以文吏治軍，明賞罰，均甘苦，尤能知人。

translations.literal: Dihui as a civil official commanded troops, made rewards and punishments clear, shared hardships equally, and especially knew men well.
translations.idiomatic: Though a civil official, Dihui commanded troops with clear rewards and punishments, shared hardship with his men, and had a rare gift for judging talent.

sentences.zh: 剿劉八時，招撫馮子材，後立大功為名將。

translations.literal: When suppressing Liu Ba he recruited Feng Zicai who later won great merit and became a famous general.
translations.idiomatic: While suppressing Liu Ba he won over Feng Zicai, who later won great distinction and became a famous general.

sentences.zh: 何高漢乃賊何博奮之弟，推誠馭之，賴以成省河之功。

translations.literal: He Gaohan was the younger brother of the bandit He Bo; Dihui won him with sincerity and relied on him to achieve the victory on the provincial river.
translations.idiomatic: He Gaohan was the younger brother of the rebel He Bo; Dihui won his loyalty with sincerity and owed his victory on the provincial river to him.

sentences.zh: 廉州、潯州、廣州三戰，皆履險犯難，卒得大捷，尤為時稱雲。

translations.literal: The three battles at Lianzhou, Xunzhou and Guangzhou were all fought through peril and hardship yet ended in great victory—this was especially praised at the time.
translations.idiomatic: The three campaigns at Lianzhou, Xunzhou, and Guangzhou all meant facing grave danger, yet each ended in a great victory—an achievement especially praised in his day.

sentences.zh: 鄧仁堃，字厚甫，湖南武岡人。

translations.literal: Deng Renkun, style name Houfu, was a native of Wugang in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Renkun, whose style was Houfu, came from Wugang in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 道光五年拔貢，以知縣用，發四川，歷署梁山、江油、洪雅。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Daoguang he was selected xiucai and used as magistrate; sent to Sichuan, he successively acted as magistrate of Liangshan, Jiangyou and Hongya.
translations.idiomatic: Selected as a xiucai in the fifth year of Daoguang, he entered service as a magistrate and was sent to Sichuan, where he successively acted as magistrate of Liangshan, Jiangyou, and Hongya.

sentences.zh: 補綦江，調富順。

translations.literal: Appointed to Qijiang, transferred to Fushun.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to Qijiang and then transferred to Fushun.

sentences.zh: 薦卓異，以憂歸。

translations.literal: Recommended as outstanding, then returned home on mourning leave.
translations.idiomatic: Recommended as outstanding in office, he then went home to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋，入貲為知府，補江西南安，調署廣信。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he purchased office as prefect, appointed to Nan'an in Jiangxi, transferred to act as Guangxin.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he bought his way to the rank of prefect, was posted to Nan'an in Jiangxi, and was transferred to act as prefect of Guangxin.

sentences.zh: 所至皆有政聲。

translations.literal: Wherever he served he gained reputation for good administration.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he earned a reputation for sound governance.

sentences.zh: 署督糧道。

translations.literal: Acting grain transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting grain transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，粵匪趨湖南，仁堃請修省城，籌守禦。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng when Cantonese bandits pressed Hunan, Renkun requested repairs to the provincial city and preparations for defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng, as Cantonese rebels pressed into Hunan, Renkun urged repairs to the provincial capital and preparations for its defense.

sentences.zh: 三年春，賊由武漢蔽江下，九江不守。

translations.literal: In spring of the third year rebels came down the Yangtze from Wuhan; Jiujiang fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the third year the rebels swept down the Yangtze from Wuhan and Jiujiang fell.

sentences.zh: 巡撫出防，民爭遷徙，仁堃諭令安堵。

translations.literal: The governor went out to defend; the people rushed to move away; Renkun ordered them to stay peacefully in place.
translations.idiomatic: The governor went out to take the field while the people scrambled to flee; Renkun ordered them to remain where they were and keep the peace.

sentences.zh: 上守江議，請增兵扼湖口，又條上城守事宜。

translations.literal: He advanced the plan to defend the river and requested troops to hold Hukou, and also submitted a list of matters for defending the city.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a plan to hold the river, asked for more troops to block Hukou, and also laid out a detailed program for defending the city.

sentences.zh: 實授督糧道。

translations.literal: Formally appointed grain transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was formally appointed grain transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 五月，賊犯江西，會江忠源師抵九江，仁堃請巡撫疏調，且遣使迎其師。

translations.literal: In the fifth month rebels invaded Jiangxi; Jiang Zhongyuan's army arrived at Jiujiang; Renkun asked the governor to memorialize for transfer and also sent envoys to welcome his army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the rebels invaded Jiangxi; Jiang Zhongyuan's force reached Jiujiang; Renkun asked the governor to memorialize for his transfer and sent envoys to welcome his troops.

sentences.zh: 忠源至，入任城守，與仁堃語合。

translations.literal: When Zhongyuan arrived he took charge of defending the city and agreed with Renkun in counsel.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhongyuan arrived he took charge of the city's defense and found himself in full agreement with Renkun.

sentences.zh: 巡撫張芾傾心倚任，曰：「戰問江君，守問鄧君！」

translations.literal: Governor Zhang Fei relied on him wholly, saying: "For battle ask Lord Jiang; for defense ask Lord Deng!"
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zhang Fei relied on them completely, saying, "For fighting ask Lord Jiang; for holding the city ask Lord Deng!"

sentences.zh: 地雷屢發壞城，皆以力戰獲完。

translations.literal: Land mines exploded repeatedly damaging the wall but each time they held through fierce fighting and the city remained intact.
translations.idiomatic: Land mines burst again and again and damaged the walls, but each time the defenders fought fiercely and kept the city intact.

sentences.zh: 仁堃欲出奇計焚賊舟，以鄱陽知縣沈衍慶忠果有謀，令率所部千人備草船藏火藥，約期襲賊，議阻未果。

translations.literal: Renkun wanted to use a stratagem to burn rebel boats; Poyang magistrate Shen Yanqing was loyal, resolute and resourceful; he ordered him to lead his thousand men to prepare straw boats hiding gunpowder for a scheduled raid on the rebels—the plan was blocked and did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Renkun wanted to try a surprise plan to burn the rebel fleet; Poyang magistrate Shen Yanqing was loyal, resolute, and resourceful, and Renkun ordered him to lead his thousand men in preparing straw boats loaded with gunpowder for a timed strike on the rebels—the plan was blocked and never carried out.

sentences.zh: 仁堃改糧船數十艘為砲艇，募卒扼守進賢門以保餉道。

translations.literal: Renkun converted several dozen grain boats into gunboats and recruited soldiers to hold Jinxian Gate to secure the supply route.
translations.idiomatic: Renkun converted several dozen grain boats into gunboats and recruited troops to hold Jinxian Gate and keep the supply line open.

sentences.zh: 自夏徂秋乃引去。

translations.literal: From summer through autumn they then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Only from summer through autumn did they finally withdraw.

sentences.zh: 仁堃曰：「賊未受大創去，禍未已也！」

translations.literal: Renkun said: "The rebels left without receiving a heavy blow—the calamity is not over yet!"
translations.idiomatic: Renkun said, "The rebels withdrew without taking a heavy blow—the danger is not past!"

sentences.zh: 亟請大修城以備，乃督工建砲城、砲台，城上官房、營棚、軍器庫、硝磺庫、了台、望樓皆備，浚環城壕深廣各三丈，築臨壕砲台，甃石為堤閘，用銀十四萬有奇，守御之具可恃。

translations.literal: He urgently requested major wall repairs as precaution, then supervised construction of gun platforms, rampart houses, camps, arsenals, saltpeter stores, watch towers—all complete; the moat was dredged three zhang deep and wide, coastal gun platforms built along it, stone embankment sluices made, spending more than 140,000 taels of silver; defensive equipment could be relied on.
translations.idiomatic: He urgently pressed for a major repair of the walls as a precaution and supervised the building of gun emplacements, rampart quarters, camps, arsenals, saltpeter depots, watch towers, and lookout posts; the encircling moat was dredged to three zhang in depth and width, gun platforms were raised along it, and stone sluice embankments were laid in at a cost of more than 140,000 taels of silver, so that the city's defenses could be trusted.

sentences.zh: 五年，賊自湖北犯義寧，仁堃令道勇五百人往援。

translations.literal: In the fifth year rebels from Hubei invaded Yining; Renkun sent five hundred circuit braves to assist.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year rebels from Hubei attacked Yining, and Renkun sent five hundred circuit braves to its relief.

sentences.zh: 會贛州知府率勇二千至，仁堃請令駐義寧；

translations.literal: The Ganzhou prefect arrived with two thousand braves; Renkun asked that they be stationed at Yining;
translations.idiomatic: When the prefect of Ganzhou arrived with two thousand braves, Renkun asked that they be posted at Yining;

sentences.zh: 巡撫陳其邁令防饒州，仁堃曰：「義寧扼三省要衝，官民頻年固守。

translations.literal: Governor Chen Qimai ordered defense of Raozhou; Renkun said: "Yining commands the junction of three provinces; officials and people have held out for years.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Chen Qimai ordered them to defend Raozhou instead; Renkun said, "Yining sits at the choke point of three provinces, and officials and people there have held out for years.

sentences.zh: 團防為江省最，若棄不救，後將不能責官以守城，責民以團練。」

translations.literal: Militia defense is Jiangxi's finest; if we abandon rescue, afterward we cannot hold officials to defend cities or the people to militia training."
translations.idiomatic: Its militia defense is the finest in Jiangxi; if we abandon it, we will never again be able to demand that officials hold their cities or that the people maintain their militia."

sentences.zh: 力請改援，不許，僅以二百五十人往助守。

translations.literal: He strongly pleaded to change to relief; it was not granted—only two hundred fifty men were sent to help defend.
translations.idiomatic: He pleaded hard to have the troops redirected, but permission was refused—only two hundred fifty men were sent to help hold the city.

sentences.zh: 中道遇賊，潰，義寧尋陷。

translations.literal: Midway they met rebels and were routed; Yining soon fell.
translations.idiomatic: On the way they met the rebels, were routed, and Yining soon fell.

sentences.zh: 未幾，羅澤南師至，仁堃固請往攻義寧，為措餉十萬濟之，澤南尋克其城。

translations.literal: Before long Luo Zinan's army arrived; Renkun insisted on going to attack Yining, provided 100,000 taels in funds, and Zinan soon took the city.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Luo Zinan's army arrived; Renkun pressed to join the attack on Yining, raised a hundred thousand taels to support it, and Zinan soon retook the city.

sentences.zh: 十月，賊陷瑞州、臨江，圍吉安，下游賊复萃九江、湖口，南昌大震。

translations.literal: In the tenth month rebels took Ruizhou and Linjiang and besieged Ji'an; downstream rebels again gathered at Jiujiang and Hukou; Nanchang was greatly shaken.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the rebels took Ruizhou and Linjiang and besieged Ji'an; downstream rebels again massed at Jiujiang and Hukou, and Nanchang was thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 仁堃添募捍衛、保衛軍，城備益嚴。

translations.literal: Renkun added recruitment of guard and defense armies; city preparations grew stricter.
translations.idiomatic: Renkun raised additional guard and defense units, and the city's preparations grew still tighter.

sentences.zh: 曾國籓令副將周鳳山率三千五百人規臨江、瑞州，戰勝樟樹鎮。

translations.literal: Zeng Guofan ordered Vice Commander Zhou Fengshan with 3,500 men to plan recovery of Linjiang and Ruizhou; they won at Zhangshuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng Guofan ordered Vice Commander Zhou Fengshan with thirty-five hundred men to recover Linjiang and Ruizhou, and they won a victory at Zhangshuzhen.

sentences.zh: 時按察使周玉衡孤軍守吉安，仁堃請檄鳳山乘勝援吉安。

translations.literal: At the time Surveillance Commissioner Zhou Yuheng held Ji'an alone with a solitary army; Renkun requested orders for Fengshan to press victory and relieve Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance Commissioner Zhou Yuheng was then holding Ji'an with a lone force; Renkun asked that orders be sent for Fengshan to press his victory and relieve Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 眾議倚鳳山蔽省城，仁堃爭曰：「賊知城高池深難卒攻，必為翦枝及本之計，先擾郡縣，使會城孤立，然後大舉而攻之。

translations.literal: Public opinion relied on Fengshan to shield the provincial capital; Renkun argued: "The rebels know the walls are high and the moat deep and hard to take quickly; they will surely cut branches then strike the root—first harry the prefectures and counties, leave the capital isolated, then mount a major assault.
translations.idiomatic: Most opinion favored keeping Fengshan to shield the provincial capital; Renkun objected: "The rebels know our walls are high and our moat deep and will not try a quick assault; they will cut the branches before striking the root—first harry the prefectures and counties, isolate the capital, and only then mount a full attack.

sentences.zh: 若懸賞二萬金，周軍必賈勇以解吉安圍，瑞、臨皆可復。

translations.literal: If we offer a reward of twenty thousand taels, Zhou's army will surely risk themselves to lift the Ji'an siege and Ruizhou and Linjiang can both be recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Offer a reward of twenty thousand taels and Zhou's men will surely risk themselves to lift the siege of Ji'an; Ruizhou and Linjiang can both be recovered.

sentences.zh: 吉安失，則撫、建必相繼不保，馴至全省糜爛，會垣且坐困矣。」

translations.literal: If Ji'an falls then Fu and Jian will surely fall in succession, until the whole province is ruined and the governor's seat is trapped.
translations.idiomatic: If Ji'an falls, Fuzhou and Jianchang will surely follow, until the whole province is laid waste and the governor's seat itself is trapped."

sentences.zh: 終不聽。

translations.literal: In the end they did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: In the end they would not listen.

sentences.zh: 六年正月，吉安陷，周玉衡死之，鳳山軍潰於樟樹鎮，撫州、建昌亦陷，南昌屬縣並為賊躪。

translations.literal: In the first month of the sixth year Ji'an fell, Zhou Yuheng died in the fighting, Fengshan's army routed at Zhangshuzhen, Fuzhou and Jianchang also fell, and all counties subject to Nanchang were overrun by rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the sixth year Ji'an fell and Zhou Yuheng died in the fighting; Fengshan's army was routed at Zhangshuzhen; Fuzhou and Jianchang also fell; and every county under Nanchang was overrun by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 仁堃兼署按察使、布政使。

translations.literal: Renkun also acted as surveillance commissioner and administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Renkun also served concurrently as surveillance commissioner and administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 子輔綸，偕同知林源恩同率平江勇三千餘人，益以寶勇、志同軍進規撫州，復進賢。

translations.literal: His son Fulu joined Sub-Prefect Lin Yuan'en in jointly leading more than three thousand Pingjiang braves, adding Bao and Zhitong armies to plan recovery of Fuzhou and advance on Jinxian.
translations.idiomatic: His son Fulu joined Sub-Prefect Lin Yuan'en in leading more than three thousand Pingjiang braves, reinforced by the Bao and Zhitong forces, in a campaign to recover Fuzhou and advance on Jinxian.

sentences.zh: 國籓亦檄李元度率勇四千自湖口移師會之，復東鄉，兩軍合破賊河東灣。

translations.literal: Guofan also ordered Li Yuandu with four thousand braves to move from Hukou to join them; they recovered Dongxiang; the two armies jointly broke the rebels at Hedongwan.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan also ordered Li Yuandu with four thousand braves to move up from Hukou to join them; they retook Dongxiang, and the two armies together defeated the rebels at Hedongwan.

sentences.zh: 攻撫州久不下，援賊驟至，營陷，林源恩死之。

translations.literal: The attack on Fuzhou was long unsuccessful; relief rebels arrived suddenly; the camp fell and Lin Yuan'en died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: The assault on Fuzhou dragged on without success; rebel reinforcements arrived suddenly, the camp was overrun, and Lin Yuan'en was killed.

sentences.zh: 學政廉兆綸劾輔綸臬司子，不應與兵事，並劾仁堃辦城工不實，事下國籓及巡撫文俊按治，坐修城時未先請勘估，降五級調用。

translations.literal: Education Intendant Lian Zhaolun impeached Fulu as the son of a surveillance commissioner who should not engage in military affairs, and also impeached Renkun for false work on city projects; the matter went to Guofan and Governor Wen Jun for investigation; they found that when repairing the wall he had not first requested survey and estimate, and he was reduced five ranks and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: Education Intendant Lian Zhaolun impeached Fulu as the son of a surveillance commissioner who ought not to take part in military affairs, and also impeached Renkun for irregularities in the city works; the case went to Guofan and Governor Wen Jun for investigation; because he had not obtained a survey and cost estimate before repairing the walls, he was reduced five ranks and transferred.

sentences.zh: 國籓疏言：「仁堃所承修為南數省第一名城。

translations.literal: Guofan memorialized: "What Renkun undertook to repair was the foremost city wall in the southern provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Guofan wrote in memorial: "What Renkun rebuilt was the foremost walled city in the southern provinces.

sentences.zh: 七郡並陷，省垣終保，不為無功。

translations.literal: Seven prefectures fell but the provincial capital was preserved to the end—not without merit.
translations.idiomatic: Seven prefectures fell, yet the provincial capital was held to the end—this was not without merit.

sentences.zh: ​​」仁堃既歸，輸穀三千石助軍。

translations.literal: After Renkun returned home he contributed three thousand shi of grain to aid the army.
translations.idiomatic: After Renkun returned home he contributed three thousand shi of grain to support the army.

sentences.zh: 十年，協守武岡，以功議敘。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he helped defend Wugang and merit was entered for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he helped defend Wugang, and his achievements were entered for official recognition.

sentences.zh: 同治五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tongzhi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Tongzhi.

sentences.zh: 余炳燾，字吟香，浙江會稽人。

translations.literal: Yu Bingtao, style name Yinxang, was a native of Kuaiji in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Bingtao, whose style was Yinxang, came from Kuaiji in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 道光元年舉人，充景山官學教習。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he passed the provincial examination and served as instructor at the Jingshan official school.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the first year of Daoguang and served as an instructor at the Jingshan official school.

sentences.zh: 期滿，以知縣用，分發陝西。

translations.literal: When his term ended he was used as magistrate and assigned to Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he entered service as a magistrate and was posted to Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 補清澗，調盩厔，又調渭南。

translations.literal: Appointed to Qingjian, transferred to Zhouzhi, then transferred to Weinan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to Qingjian, transferred to Zhouzhi, and then to Weinan.

sentences.zh: 回人馬得全等謀不軌，親入其巢捕之，置諸法，擢河南懷慶知府。

translations.literal: The Muslims Ma Dequan and others plotted sedition; he personally entered their nest to capture them and punished them by law; he was promoted to prefect of Huaqing in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Muslims Ma Dequan and others plotted rebellion, he went in person into their stronghold to seize them, had them punished by law, and was promoted to prefect of Huaqing in Henan.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，粵匪北犯窺開封，遂渡河圍懷慶。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng Cantonese bandits pressed north toward Kaifeng, then crossed the river and besieged Huaqing.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng the Cantonese rebels marched north toward Kaifeng, crossed the river, and besieged Huaqing.

sentences.zh: 時郡城兵僅三百，炳燾選團勇三千人登陴固守，募敢死士縋城下砍賊營，又潛毒城外汲道使自斃。

translations.literal: At the time the prefectural city had only three hundred troops; Bingtao selected three thousand militia to mount the walls and hold fast, recruited dare-to-die men to be lowered down the walls to cut at rebel camps, and secretly poisoned the water sources outside the city so the rebels poisoned themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectural city then had only three hundred regular troops; Bingtao chose three thousand militiamen to man the walls, recruited dare-to-die squads to be lowered over the walls to strike rebel camps, and secretly poisoned the wells outside so the rebels poisoned themselves.

sentences.zh: 賊以地雷隳城者三，皆擊退。

translations.literal: The rebels used land mines to breach the wall three times; each time they were beaten back.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels used land mines to breach the walls three times, and each time they were driven back.

sentences.zh: 一日，雷雨中砲火蝟集，危甚，天忽反風，賊燔死者眾，勢頓沮。

translations.literal: One day in thunder and rain cannon fire gathered thickly and the danger was extreme; heaven suddenly reversed the wind and many rebels were burned to death; their momentum abruptly collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: One day, amid thunder and rain, cannon fire converged from every side and the danger was extreme; then the wind suddenly shifted, many rebels were burned alive, and their momentum collapsed.

sentences.zh: 賊於近城樹木柵，以斷內外，為久困計。

translations.literal: The rebels erected wooden palisades near the city to cut off inside from outside, planning a long siege.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels built wooden palisades near the walls to sever the city from the outside, intending a long blockade.

sentences.zh: 山東巡撫李僡先赴援，既而援軍四集，詔大學士訥爾經額督師。

translations.literal: Shandong Governor Li Yun went first to relieve; afterward relief armies gathered from four directions; the emperor ordered Grand Secretary Ne'erjing'e to command the army.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong Governor Li Yun was the first to come to the relief; soon relief forces gathered from all sides, and the court ordered Grand Secretary Ne'erjing'e to take command.

sentences.zh: 圍久，城中糧漸不支，炳燾素得民心，激以忠義，括糧節食，人心不渙。

translations.literal: The siege was long and grain in the city gradually failed; Bingtao had always won the people's hearts; he roused them with loyalty and righteousness, collected grain and economized food, and popular morale did not scatter.
translations.idiomatic: As the siege dragged on, food in the city ran low; Bingtao had long enjoyed the people's trust; he stirred them with talk of loyalty and duty, pooled grain and rationed food, and morale held firm.

sentences.zh: 屢詔促戰，都統勝保、將軍托明阿等迭敗賊，賊始入山西竄，凡被圍五十八日乃解。

translations.literal: Repeated edicts urged battle; Banner Commander Shengbao, General Tuoming'a and others defeated the rebels in succession; the rebels then fled into Shanxi; the siege lasted fifty-eight days before it was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Edict after edict urged an offensive; Banner Commander Shengbao, General Tuoming'a, and others defeated the rebels in turn; the rebels then fled into Shanxi; the siege had lasted fifty-eight days before it was raised.

sentences.zh: 特詔褒獎，賜花翎，以道員用，擢陝西鳳邠道。

translations.literal: A special edict praised and rewarded him, granted peacock feathers, used him as circuit intendant, and promoted him to Fengbin Circuit of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: A special edict praised his service, granted him peacock feathers, appointed him to circuit rank, and promoted him to intendant of Fengbin Circuit in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 尋改授河南南汝光道。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Nanyuguang Circuit of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to Nanyuguang Circuit in Henan.

sentences.zh: 未幾，就遷按察使。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted in place to surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 大河南北以防匪倡聯莊會，遇警相救；

translations.literal: North and south of the Great River in Henan, to guard against bandits they promoted village associations that aided one another in emergencies;
translations.idiomatic: Across Henan north and south of the Yellow River, villages formed mutual-aid associations to guard against bandits;

sentences.zh: 及賊去，聚而不散，莠民恃眾抗官。

translations.literal: when the bandits left they gathered but did not disperse; bad elements relied on their numbers to resist officials.
translations.idiomatic: but after the rebels withdrew the groups stayed together, and ruffians used their numbers to defy the authorities.

sentences.zh: 四年，禹州、鄭州、密縣疊肇變，圍城、焚署、縱囚、掠紳民。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Yuzhou, Zhengzhou and Mixian erupted in disturbances one after another, besieging cities, burning yamens, freeing prisoners and plundering gentry and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Yuzhou, Zhengzhou, and Mixian rose in succession—besieging cities, burning government offices, freeing prisoners, and plundering gentry and commoners.

sentences.zh: 巡撫英桂出防信陽，咸請兩司奏聞待命。

translations.literal: Governor Yinggui went out to defend Xinyang; all asked the two commissioners to memorialize and await orders.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Yinggui went out to defend Xinyang, and everyone urged the two provincial commissioners to memorialize the throne and wait for orders.

sentences.zh: 炳燾曰：「賊雖眾，皆烏合，志在剽掠，無紀律。

translations.literal: Bingtao said: "Though the bandits are numerous, they are all a rabble, intent on plunder, without discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Bingtao said, "Though they are numerous, these are a rabble intent only on loot, without discipline.

sentences.zh: 速臨以兵，必驚潰，解散其黨，不久魁渠可縛也。

translations.literal: If we quickly come upon them with troops they will surely panic and scatter; break up their bands and before long the chiefs can be bound.
translations.idiomatic: Move on them quickly with troops and they will panic and scatter; break up their bands and their leaders can soon be taken.

sentences.zh: 若請朝命，遲將蔓延！」

translations.literal: If we request court orders, delay will let it spread!"
translations.idiomatic: If we wait for court orders, the trouble will spread before we act!"

sentences.zh: 遂親率兵七百、勇五百馳往，剿撫兼施，事即定。

translations.literal: Thereupon he personally led seven hundred troops and five hundred braves in a rapid march; suppression and pacification together were applied and the matter was settled at once.
translations.idiomatic: He then led seven hundred regular troops and five hundred braves in person; combining force with conciliation, he settled the affair at once.

sentences.zh: 尋署布政使。

translations.literal: Soon he acted as administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He soon served as acting administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 捻首張洛行擾歸德，命炳燾往剿，攻雉河集，解亳州圍，又潛入永城，擊走之。

translations.literal: Nian chief Zhang Luoxing harassed Guide; Bingtao was ordered to suppress him, attacked Zhiheji, lifted the siege of Bozhou, and also slipped into Yongcheng and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: When Nian leader Zhang Luoxing harassed Guide, Bingtao was ordered against him; he attacked Zhiheji, lifted the siege of Bozhou, slipped into Yongcheng, and drove the rebels off.

sentences.zh: 既而歸德又有警，炳燾馳救，而他軍遽退，賊遂東逸。

translations.literal: Before long Guide was alarmed again; Bingtao raced to rescue, but other armies abruptly withdrew and the bandits fled east.
translations.idiomatic: Guide was soon threatened again; Bingtao rushed to its aid, but other units pulled back abruptly and the rebels escaped eastward.

sentences.zh: 炳燾染病，特旨予假治理，不開缺。

translations.literal: Bingtao fell ill; a special edict granted leave for treatment without vacating his post.
translations.idiomatic: Bingtao fell ill; a special edict granted him leave for treatment without vacating his post.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the seventh year.

sentences.zh: 懷慶請祀名宦祠。

translations.literal: Huaqing requested his enshrinement in the shrine of eminent officials.
translations.idiomatic: Huaqing petitioned to enshrine him in the local shrine of eminent officials.

sentences.zh: 栗燿，字仲然，山西渾源人，東河總督毓美子。

translations.literal: Li Yao, style name Zhongran, was a native of Hunyuan in Shanxi, son of Grand Canal Director Yumei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yao, whose style was Zhongran, came from Hunyuan in Shanxi and was the son of Grand Canal Director Yumei.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年舉人，以父血卩廕，特賜進士。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he passed the provincial examination; because of his father's blood memorial he was specially granted jinshi.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the fifteenth year of Daoguang and, through his father's blood memorial, was specially granted the jinshi degree.

sentences.zh: 咸豐三年，授湖北漢陽知府，至則漢陽再陷，行省未復，督撫皆寄治軍中，委燿綜理營務。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianfeng he was appointed prefect of Hanyang in Hubei; on arrival Hanyang had fallen again, the provincial seat was not recovered, governor and governor-general all lodged with the army, and Yao was entrusted to manage camp affairs comprehensively.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianfeng he was appointed prefect of Hanyang in Hubei; when he arrived Hanyang had fallen again, the provincial capital was still lost, and the governor and governor-general were both encamped with the army, so Yao was put in charge of camp affairs.

sentences.zh: 四年，從大軍复武漢，未幾，賊大至，城复陷，六年，始復。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed the great army to recover Wuhan; before long rebels came in force and the city fell again; only in the sixth year was it recovered.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he followed the main army in retaking Wuhan; soon the rebels returned in force and the city fell again; it was not recovered until the sixth year.

sentences.zh: 敘功，晉秩道員。

translations.literal: Merit was entered and he was advanced to circuit intendant rank.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were recorded and he was raised to circuit intendant rank.

sentences.zh: 燿以廉幹為巡撫胡林翼所器，令筦釐稅糧台。

translations.literal: Yao for his integrity and capability was valued by Governor Hu Linyi, who ordered him to manage the likin tax and grain bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Valued by Governor Hu Linyi for his integrity and efficiency, Yao was put in charge of the likin tax and grain bureau.

sentences.zh: 八年，署荊宜施道。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he acted as Jingyi-Shi Circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he served as acting intendant of Jingyi-Shi Circuit.

sentences.zh: 尋加按察使銜，授武昌道，仍留署任，兼督鈔關。

translations.literal: Soon he was given surveillance commissioner rank, appointed to Wuchang Circuit, still retained in his acting post, and also supervised the paper-money customs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given the rank of surveillance commissioner, appointed to Wuchang Circuit while kept in his acting post, and also placed in charge of the paper-money customs.

sentences.zh: 軍餉皆仰資鹽榷，燿綜核嚴密，稅入羨餘，悉籍入公。

translations.literal: Army funds all relied on the salt monopoly; Yao audited strictly; tax surpluses were all entered into public accounts.
translations.idiomatic: Army funds depended entirely on the salt monopoly; Yao audited accounts with great strictness, and every surplus in tax receipts was entered into the public ledger.

sentences.zh: 修戰艦，增軍屯，水陸戰守皆有備。

translations.literal: He repaired warships, increased military colonies; land and water, attack and defense were all provided for.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired warships, expanded military colonies, and made ready for both land and water, offense and defense.

sentences.zh: 十一年，賊逼施南，燿請重兵，复集民團，守山險。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year rebels pressed Shinan; Yao requested heavy troops, again gathered militia, and held mountain passes.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year rebels pressed Shinan; Yao asked for reinforcements, rallied the militia again, and held the mountain passes.

sentences.zh: 賊合川匪分掠宣、咸諸縣，施南協副將御之，遇伏，一軍盡沒。

translations.literal: Rebels joined Sichuan bandits to plunder Xuan, Xian and other counties; the Shinan assistant regional commander met them and fell into an ambush; the whole force was wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels joined Sichuan bandits to raid Xuan, Xian, and other counties; the assistant regional commander of Shinan met them, was ambushed, and his entire force was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 會劉岳昭軍至，與郡兵夾擊，賊大創，竄歸。

translations.literal: When Liu Yuezhao's army arrived it attacked from both sides with prefectural troops; the rebels suffered a heavy blow and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yuezhao's army arrived it struck the rebels from both sides with the prefectural troops; the rebels were badly mauled and fled back.

sentences.zh: 松滋人馬鉦者，挾左道惑人，眾至數千，密通賊，官軍擒斬之。

translations.literal: Ma Zheng of Songzi practiced heterodox ways to delude people; his followers reached several thousand; he secretly communicated with rebels; government troops captured and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zheng of Songzi used heterodox teachings to mislead the people until his following numbered thousands; he secretly colluded with the rebels until government troops captured and executed him.

sentences.zh: 燿料賊不知鉦死，必復至，集水陸軍密為備。

translations.literal: Yao judged that the rebels did not know Zheng was dead and would surely come again; he gathered land and water forces and secretly made preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Yao reckoned the rebels did not yet know Zheng was dead and would return; he gathered land and river forces and made secret preparations.

sentences.zh: 賊果趣夔州，遇官軍輒敗，及知馬鉦已誅，遂大潰。

translations.literal: The rebels indeed hurried toward Kuizhou; whenever they met government troops they were defeated; when they learned Ma Zheng had been executed they broke in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels did hurry toward Kuizhou, but were beaten whenever they met government troops; when they learned Ma Zheng had been killed, they broke and fled in disorder.

sentences.zh: 水陸合擊，俘斬萬餘，自是川匪無敢犯楚境。

translations.literal: Land and water forces attacked together; more than ten thousand were captured or beheaded; from then Sichuan bandits dared not invade Chu territory.
translations.idiomatic: Land and river forces struck together, taking or killing more than ten thousand; after that Sichuan bandits no longer dared cross into Hubei.

sentences.zh: 會大雨，荊江暴漲，齧攻萬城堤。

translations.literal: Heavy rain fell; the Jing River rose in flood and gnawed at the Wancheng embankment.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy rains came, the Jing River swelled in flood, and the current began to eat away the Wancheng embankment.

sentences.zh: 燿督兵民備畚挶，儲土石，立泥淖間躬視板築，信宿堤上，事定乃還。

translations.literal: Yao supervised soldiers and people in preparing baskets and shovels, storing earth and stone; he stood in the mud to oversee piling and building himself, spent two nights on the embankment, and returned only when the matter was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Yao directed soldiers and civilians in preparing tools and stockpiling earth and stone; he stood in the mud to oversee the work in person, spent two nights on the embankment, and returned only when the danger had passed.

sentences.zh: 在荊州四年，政教大行。

translations.literal: During four years at Jingzhou government and teaching flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: During his four years at Jingzhou, government and public instruction flourished.

sentences.zh: 署按察使，兼攝布政使，甫踰月，授湖北按察使。

translations.literal: He acted as surveillance commissioner and also held administration commissioner; barely a month passed before he was appointed Hubei surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting surveillance commissioner and also held the administration commissioner's post; barely a month later he was appointed surveillance commissioner of Hubei.

sentences.zh: 燿以其父毓美曾任是職，乃顏其堂曰誦芬。

translations.literal: Yao because his father Yumei had once held this post inscribed his hall with the name "Reciting Fragrance."
translations.idiomatic: Because his father Yumei had once held the same post, Yao named his hall Reciting Fragrance.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，擢布政使，未任，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was promoted administration commissioner but did not take office before he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he was promoted to administration commissioner but died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 硃孫貽，字石翹，江西清江人。

translations.literal: Zhu Sunyi, style name Shiqiao, was a native of Qingjiang in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Sunyi, whose style was Shiqiao, came from Qingjiang in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 入貲為刑部主事。

translations.literal: He purchased office as a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He bought his way into office as a principal clerk in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 改知縣，發湖南，歷署寧鄉、長沙，皆有聲。

translations.literal: He changed to magistrate, was sent to Hunan, and successively acted as magistrate of Ningxiang and Changsha, gaining reputation everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to the magistracy, he was posted to Hunan and successively acted as magistrate of Ningxiang and Changsha, earning a good name in each post.

sentences.zh: 道光三十年，署湘鄉。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Daoguang he acted as magistrate of Xiangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year of Daoguang he served as acting magistrate of Xiangxiang.

sentences.zh: 漕務積弊，屢釀巨獄，孫貽蒞任，鄉民方麕集環譟。

translations.literal: Grain transport had long-standing abuses that repeatedly produced major cases; when Sunyi took office the villagers were just gathering in crowds and shouting all around.
translations.idiomatic: The grain-transport service was riddled with long-standing abuses that had repeatedly led to major cases; when Sunyi took office the villagers were already gathering in angry crowds.

sentences.zh: 孫貽令曰：「新漕限迫，驟改章，弗及。

translations.literal: Sunyi ordered: "The new grain transport deadline is pressing; to change regulations abruptly is not possible.
translations.idiomatic: Sunyi proclaimed, "The deadline for the new grain levy is upon us; regulations cannot be changed overnight.

sentences.zh: 來年當為若剔朘削弊，敢煽動浮言者罪之。

translations.literal: Next year I shall pare abuses for you; whoever dares stir up loose talk will be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Next year I will cut the abuses down for you; anyone who stirs up trouble with loose talk will be punished.

sentences.zh: 會匪切近災也，亟縛獻！」

translations.literal: The bandits are close upon disaster; bind them quickly and present them!"
translations.idiomatic: The bandits are at our very gates—seize them and bring them in at once!"

sentences.zh: 眾唯唯散。

translations.literal: The crowd murmured assent and dispersed.
translations.idiomatic: The crowd murmured agreement and dispersed.

sentences.zh: 疊捕盜魁陳勝祥、劉福田等置之法。

translations.literal: He captured in succession the bandit chiefs Chen Shengxiang, Liu Futian and others and punished them by law.
translations.idiomatic: He captured one bandit chief after another—Chen Shengxiang, Liu Futian, and others—and punished them by law.

sentences.zh: 稔知邑士之賢者，舉羅澤南孝廉方正；

translations.literal: Well knowing the worthy scholars of the county, he recommended Luo Zinan as filial and incorrupt;
translations.idiomatic: Knowing well the able men of the county, he recommended Luo Zinan as a candidate for filial and incorrupt office;

sentences.zh: 縣試拔劉蓉冠其曹；

translations.literal: at the county examination he ranked Liu Rong first in his class;
translations.idiomatic: at the county examination he placed Liu Rong at the head of his class;

sentences.zh: 延王珍襄幕；

translations.literal: he invited Wang Zhen to assist in his secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: he invited Wang Zhen to join his staff;

sentences.zh: 於康景暉、李續賓、續宜皆獎勗之。

translations.literal: to Kang Jinghui, Li Xubin and Xuyi he all gave encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: and he encouraged Kang Jinghui, Li Xubin, and Xuyi alike.

sentences.zh: 廣西匪熾，孫貽集眾曰：「賊勢未易殄，北竄，湖南當其衝，欲衛閭里，非團練鄉兵不可。」

translations.literal: Guangxi bandits blazed; Sunyi gathered the assembly and said: "The rebel force is not easily destroyed; fleeing north, Hunan lies in their path; to defend our neighborhoods, militia and village soldiers are indispensable."
translations.idiomatic: As Guangxi rebels grew fierce, Sunyi assembled the people and said, "These rebels will not be easily destroyed; if they flee north, Hunan will bear the brunt—to defend our homes we must rely on militia and village troops."

sentences.zh: 王珍等曰：「謹奉令！」

translations.literal: Wang Zhen and others said: "We respectfully obey!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen and the others replied, "We obey!"

sentences.zh: 總督程矞採防衡州，孫貽以策乾之，不省。

translations.literal: Governor Cheng Yucai defended Hengzhou; Sunyi presented a plan to him but he did not heed it.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Cheng Yucai was defending Hengzhou; Sunyi submitted a plan to him, but it went unheeded.

sentences.zh: 會匪驟起，偕劉蓉、康景暉往捕。

translations.literal: Bandits suddenly rose; he went with Liu Rong and Kang Jinghui to capture them.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits suddenly rose, he went with Liu Rong and Kang Jinghui to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 孫貽中彈，裹創戰於湖洞，擒賊目王祥二、熊聰一，王珍复捕賊百餘，檻致總督行營，前後七百餘人。

translations.literal: Sunyi was struck by a bullet; binding his wound he fought at Hudong, captured rebel leaders Wang Xiang'er and Xiong Congyi; Wang Zhen again captured more than a hundred bandits; they were caged and sent to the governor's camp—more than seven hundred in all before and after.
translations.idiomatic: Sunyi was shot but bound his wound and kept fighting at Hudong; he captured the rebel leaders Wang Xiang'er and Xiong Congyi; Wang Zhen took more than a hundred more; in all more than seven hundred were sent in cages to the governor's camp.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，洪秀全連陷道州、江華、永明、桂陽、郴州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng Hong Xiuquan captured in succession Daozhou, Jianghua, Yongming, Guiyang and Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianfeng Hong Xiuquan took Daozhou, Jianghua, Yongming, Guiyang, and Chenzhou in succession.

sentences.zh: 孫貽集團丁分三營，以羅澤南領中營，易良幹副之；

translations.literal: Sunyi gathered militia and divided them into three battalions; Luo Zinan led the center battalion with Yi Lianggan as his deputy;
translations.idiomatic: Sunyi gathered the militia into three battalions: Luo Zinan commanded the center battalion with Yi Lianggan as his deputy;

sentences.zh: 王珍領左營，揚虎臣、王開化、張運蘭隸焉；

translations.literal: Wang Zhen led the left battalion with Yang Huchen, Wang Kaihua and Zhang Yunlan under him;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhen led the left battalion with Yang Huchen, Wang Kaihua, and Zhang Yunlan under him;

sentences.zh: 康景暉領右營。

translations.literal: Kang Jinghui led the right battalion.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Jinghui led the right battalion.

sentences.zh: 羅信南綜糧糈，謝邦翰治兵械。

translations.literal: Luo Xinnan managed provisions; Xie Banghan managed weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Xinnan handled provisions while Xie Banghan handled arms.

sentences.zh: 推古人陣法，制為起伏分合，湘軍紀律自此始。

translations.literal: He applied ancient battle formations, devised advance and retreat with division and union; Xiang Army discipline began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on ancient battle formations, he devised tactics of advance, retreat, division, and reunion—the disciplined Xiang Army began here.

sentences.zh: 長沙圍未解，王珍、康景暉、趙煥聯分駐要隘；

translations.literal: The siege of Changsha was not yet lifted; Wang Zhen, Kang Jinghui and Zhao Huanlian were posted separately at key passes;
translations.idiomatic: While Changsha was still besieged, Wang Zhen, Kang Jinghui, and Zhao Huanlian held key passes;

sentences.zh: 羅澤南、易良幹防縣城，伏莽蠢動，即時捕滅，縣境肅然。

translations.literal: Luo Zinan and Yi Lianggan defended the county seat; hidden ruffians stirred but were captured and destroyed at once; the county was orderly.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Zinan and Yi Lianggan defended the county seat; hidden ruffians stirred but were crushed at once, and the county was kept quiet.

sentences.zh: 三年，巡撫張亮基聞湘鄉團丁名，調防省城，孫貽令王珍、羅澤南、羅信南、劉蓉率之往。

translations.literal: In the third year Governor Zhang Liangji heard the fame of Xiangxiang militia and transferred them to defend the provincial capital; Sunyi ordered Wang Zhen, Luo Zinan, Luo Xinnan and Liu Rong to lead them there.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Governor Zhang Liangji heard of the Xiangxiang militia's reputation and called them to defend the provincial capital; Sunyi sent Wang Zhen, Luo Zinan, Luo Xinnan, and Liu Rong to lead them.

sentences.zh: 四年，孫貽率團破安化藍田賊，擢郴州直隸州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Sunyi led the militia to defeat bandits at Anhua and Lantian; he was promoted to direct-administration prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Sunyi led the militia to defeat bandits in Anhua and Lantian and was promoted to direct-administration prefect of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 江忠源奉幫辦軍務之命，與曾國籓議援江西，令孫貽率湘軍赴之。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhongyuan received orders to assist in military affairs; with Zeng Guofan he discussed aiding Jiangxi and ordered Sunyi to lead the Xiang Army there.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to assist in military affairs, Jiang Zhongyuan discussed relief for Jiangxi with Zeng Guofan and sent Sunyi at the head of the Xiang Army.

sentences.zh: 羅澤南領中營，易良幹領前營，謝邦翰領右營，康景暉領左營，揚虎臣領後營，羅信南領親兵營，共三千人，至南昌，戰永定門外，大破賊。

translations.literal: Luo Zinan led the center battalion, Yi Lianggan the vanguard, Xie Banghan the right, Kang Jinghui the left, Yang Huchen the rear, Luo Xinnan the personal guard battalion—three thousand in all; they reached Nanchang, fought outside Yongding Gate and inflicted a great defeat on the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Zinan commanded the center, Yi Lianggan the vanguard, Xie Banghan the right, Kang Jinghui the left, Yang Huchen the rear, and Luo Xinnan the personal guard—three thousand men in all; they reached Nanchang, fought outside Yongding Gate, and won a crushing victory.

sentences.zh: 謝邦翰、易良幹、羅信東窮追被戕，孫貽哭之慟，以李續賓代領右營，羅信南兼領前營。

translations.literal: Xie Banghan, Yi Lianggan and Luo Xindong were killed in hot pursuit; Sunyi mourned them bitterly; Li Xubin was put in command of the right battalion and Luo Xinnan also took the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Banghan, Yi Lianggan, and Luo Xindong were killed in the pursuit; Sunyi mourned them deeply; Li Xubin took over the right battalion and Luo Xinnan the vanguard as well.

sentences.zh: 吉安土匪鄒恩隆應賊，孫貽扼樟樹鎮，分軍令澤南、續賓及劉長佑剿平之。

translations.literal: Ji'an bandit Zou Enlong joined the rebels; Sunyi held Zhangshuzhen and divided his army, ordering Zinan, Xubin and Liu Changyou to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: The Ji'an bandit Zou Enlong joined the rebels; Sunyi held Zhangshuzhen and detached forces under Zinan, Xubin, and Liu Changyou to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 南昌圍解，凱旋，加知府銜，擢寶慶知府。

translations.literal: The siege of Nanchang was lifted; returning in triumph he was given prefect rank and promoted to prefect of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: When the siege of Nanchang was lifted he returned in triumph, was given prefect rank, and was appointed prefect of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 諏才俊，嚴保甲，懲積匪，一如治湘鄉時。

translations.literal: He sought out talented men, enforced the baojia system strictly, punished long-standing bandits—just as when governing Xiangxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He sought out talent, enforced the baojia system strictly, and punished entrenched bandits just as he had in Xiangxiang.

sentences.zh: 捐寺觀貲產製旗械軍火，募戰士千人，發義倉、常平儲穀充餉，親歷各鄉訓練，捕新寧山門團匪誅之。

translations.literal: He donated temple and monastery assets to make banners, weapons and munitions, recruited a thousand warriors, issued grain from charity granaries and ever-normal granaries for pay, personally went through each township for training, and captured and executed the Xinning Shanmen militia bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He used temple and monastery funds to make banners, arms, and munitions, recruited a thousand fighters, drew grain from charity and ever-normal granaries for pay, trained the militia in each township in person, and captured and executed the Xinning Shanmen bandits.

sentences.zh: 五年，粵匪陷東安，率千人偕副將聯霈馳扼五峰鋪，賊不敢犯。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Cantonese bandits took Dong'an; he led a thousand men with Vice Commander Lian Pei in a rapid march to hold Wufengpu; the rebels dared not invade.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Cantonese rebels took Dong'an; he led a thousand men with Vice Commander Lian Pei to hold Wufengpu, and the rebels did not dare advance.

sentences.zh: 衡陽土匪起，出境平之。

translations.literal: Hengyang bandits rose; he went beyond the border and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Hengyang he crossed the border and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 六年，駱秉章疏薦人才，記名以湖南道員簡放。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Luo Bingzhang memorialized recommending talent; Sunyi was registered for appointment as Hunan circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Luo Bingzhang memorialized recommending men of talent, and Sunyi was registered for appointment as a Hunan circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 尋以治防功被優敘。

translations.literal: Soon for his merit in governing defense he received preferential entry in the records.
translations.idiomatic: Soon his achievements in organizing defense were entered for special recognition.

sentences.zh: 八年，勞崇光調赴廣西，假滿未出，降一級調用，仍治湘、寶團防。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Lao Chongguang transferred him to Guangxi; when his leave ended he did not go out; he was reduced one rank and transferred, still governing militia defense in Xiang and Bao.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Lao Chongguang ordered him to Guangxi; when his leave expired he did not go; he was reduced one rank and transferred but still oversaw militia defense in Xiangxiang and Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 十年，會劉長佑克廣西柳州，開復處分，賜花翎，加按察使銜。

translations.literal: In the tenth year when Liu Changyou took Liuzhou in Guangxi, his penalties were lifted, peacock feathers were granted, and surveillance commissioner rank was added.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, when Liu Changyou took Liuzhou in Guangxi, his penalties were lifted, he was granted peacock feathers, and given the rank of surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 駱秉章赴四川督師，奏調孫貽總理營務。

translations.literal: Luo Bingzhang went to Sichuan to command the army and memorialized to transfer Sunyi to manage camp affairs comprehensively.
translations.idiomatic: When Luo Bingzhang went to Sichuan to take command, he memorialized to have Sunyi placed in charge of camp affairs.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，擢授浙江鹽運使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was promoted and appointed Zhejiang salt transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he was promoted to Zhejiang salt transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 秉章奏治川省團練，孫貽與秉章左右議不合，引疾請罷。

translations.literal: Bingzhang memorialized on governing Sichuan militia; Sunyi disagreed with Bingzhang's close advisers and cited illness to request dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: Bingzhang memorialized on organizing Sichuan militia; Sunyi clashed with Bingzhang's advisers and asked to be relieved on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 命力疾赴陝西佐理多隆阿營務，以病辭，終不復出。

translations.literal: He was ordered to go despite illness to Shaanxi to assist Duo Long'a in camp affairs; he declined on grounds of illness and never served again.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to go to Shaanxi despite his illness to assist Duo Long'a in camp affairs; he declined on grounds of sickness and never took office again.

sentences.zh: 光緒五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Guangxu he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Guangxu.

sentences.zh: 史致諤，字士良，順天宛平人，原籍江蘇溧陽。

translations.literal: Shi Zhie, style name Shiliang, was a native of Wanping in Shuntian, original domicile Liyang in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhie, whose style was Shiliang, was registered in Wanping in Shuntian but came from Liyang in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 道光十八年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the eighteenth year of Daoguang, was chosen as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 道光末，出為江西廣信知府。

translations.literal: At the end of Daoguang he went out as prefect of Guangxin in Jiangxi.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Daoguang reign he was sent out as prefect of Guangxin in Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，署南昌。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he acted as magistrate of Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng he served as acting prefect of Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 三年，粵匪犯江南，九江戒嚴，南昌訛言四起，城門晝閉，致諤請開城以安人心。

translations.literal: In the third year Cantonese bandits invaded Jiangnan; Jiujiang was on alert; false rumors spread in Nanchang; city gates were closed by day; Zhie requested opening the city to calm hearts.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Cantonese rebels invaded the lower Yangtze region; Jiujiang went on alert; rumors spread through Nanchang and the gates were shut by day; Zhie urged that the city be opened to calm the people.

sentences.zh: 尋回廣信任。

translations.literal: Soon he returned to his post at Guangxin.
translations.idiomatic: He soon returned to Guangxin.

sentences.zh: 賊陷饒州，致諤募勇號信新軍，因險設防，與浙軍為犄角。

translations.literal: When rebels took Raozhou, Zhie recruited braves called the Xinxin Army, set defenses at strategic points, and formed a flank position with Zhejiang troops.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels took Raozhou, Zhie raised a force called the Xinxin Army, fortified the passes, and coordinated with Zhejiang troops as a supporting wing.

sentences.zh: 四年，調南昌。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Nanchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to Nanchang.

sentences.zh: 江西諸郡行淮鹽，惟廣信行浙鹽。

translations.literal: Jiangxi prefectures all used Huai salt; only Guangxin used Zhe salt.
translations.idiomatic: The prefectures of Jiangxi used Huai salt, but Guangxin alone used Zhe salt.

sentences.zh: 軍興，淮鹽不至，致諤議借銷浙引，以餘息充餉，名曰「餉鹽」，從之，即以致諤襄其事。

translations.literal: With the war, Huai salt did not arrive; Zhie proposed borrowing Zhe salt tickets for sale, using the surplus interest for army pay, called "pay salt"; it was approved and Zhie was put in charge.
translations.idiomatic: When war broke out Huai salt stopped coming; Zhie proposed selling Zhe salt tickets instead and using the surplus for army pay under the name "pay salt"; the plan was approved and he was put in charge.

sentences.zh: 年餘，銷引逾常額，江、楚及浙皆利之。

translations.literal: After more than a year sales of tickets exceeded the normal quota; Jiang, Chu and Zhe all benefited.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year sales exceeded the usual quota, to the benefit of the Jiang, Chu, and Zhe regions alike.

sentences.zh: 賊陷武寧，致諤率信新軍赴剿，迭挫賊於紫鹿嶺、巾口、火爐坪、箬田，复武寧。

translations.literal: When rebels took Wuning, Zhie led the Xinxin Army to suppress them, repeatedly defeating rebels at Ziluling, Jinkou, Huoluping and Ruotian, and recovered Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels took Wuning, Zhie led the Xinxin Army against them, defeated them repeatedly at Ziluling, Jinkou, Huoluping, and Ruotian, and retook Wuning.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，南昌戒嚴，援師大集，主客軍不相下。

translations.literal: That winter Nanchang was on alert; relief armies gathered in force; host and guest armies would not yield to one another.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Nanchang was placed on alert as relief armies massed; the local and outside forces refused to defer to one another.

sentences.zh: 致諤協和將吏，客軍二卒持刀擾質庫，立斬以徇。

translations.literal: Zhie harmonized officers and men; two soldiers of the guest army took knives and disturbed a pawnshop; he beheaded them at once as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhie worked to keep officers and men in harmony; when two outside soldiers armed with knives disturbed a pawnshop, he had them beheaded on the spot as a warning.

sentences.zh: 五年，兼署鹽法道。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he also acted as salt commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he also served as acting salt commissioner.

sentences.zh: 尋以母憂去官，留襄軍事。

translations.literal: Soon he left office on mourning for his mother but remained to assist military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He soon left office to mourn his mother but stayed on to assist in military affairs.

sentences.zh: 九年，服闋，命赴浙江交巡撫王有齡差遣。

translations.literal: In the ninth year when mourning ended he was ordered to Zhejiang to take orders from Governor Wang Youling.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when his mourning ended, he was ordered to Zhejiang to serve under Governor Wang Youling.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，署寧紹台道。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he acted as Ning-Shao-Tai Circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he served as acting intendant of Ning-Shao-Tai Circuit.

sentences.zh: 寧波自前歲陷於賊，資洋兵之力复城，方謀畫曹娥江而守。

translations.literal: Ningbo had fallen to rebels the year before; relying on foreign troops the city was recovered; they were just planning to hold the Cao'e River line.
translations.idiomatic: Ningbo had fallen the year before and been retaken with foreign troops; the plan was to hold the line of the Cao'e River.

sentences.zh: 尋以法總兵馬籌思所部與廣勇互鬥，廣勇潰，賊乘間竄慈谿、奉化。

translations.literal: Soon the French brigadier Ma Chousi's troops fought with Guang braves; the Guang braves routed; rebels seized the chance to slip into Cixi and Fenghua.
translations.idiomatic: Soon French Brigadier Ma Chousi's men clashed with Guangdong braves; the braves broke; and the rebels seized the chance to slip into Cixi and Fenghua.

sentences.zh: 致諤至，慈谿已陷，激厲民團登陴固守。

translations.literal: When Zhie arrived Cixi had already fallen; he roused the militia to mount the walls and hold fast.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhie arrived Cixi had already fallen; he rallied the militia to man the walls and hold firm.

sentences.zh: 與英總兵欻樂克、稅務司法人日意格推誠相結；

translations.literal: He joined in sincerity with British Brigadier Frederick Townsend Ward and French customs official Prosper Giquel;
translations.idiomatic: He formed a bond of trust with British Brigadier Frederick Townsend Ward and the French customs official Prosper Giquel;

sentences.zh: 以美兵官華爾忠勇可用，介以相見，令攻慈谿，以駐餘姚之洋兵及同知謝採璋團勇應之。

translations.literal: Judging the American officer Ward loyal and brave and usable, he introduced them; ordered Ward to attack Cixi, with foreign troops stationed at Yuyao and Sub-Prefect Xie Caizhang's militia to cooperate.
translations.idiomatic: Finding the American officer Ward loyal and capable, he brought them together and ordered Ward to attack Cixi, with foreign troops at Yuyao and Sub-Prefect Xie Caizhang's militia in support.

sentences.zh: 慈谿賊分擾鄞縣境，及半浦，而嵊縣、新昌賊復大舉犯陳公嶺。

translations.literal: Cixi rebels divided to harass Yin county as far as Banpu; meanwhile Sheng and Xinchang rebels again mounted a major attack on Chenggong Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels from Cixi raided into Yin county as far as Banpu, while rebels from Sheng and Xinchang again launched a major assault on Chenggong Ridge.

sentences.zh: 華爾克慈谿，中砲歿於軍。

translations.literal: Ward took Cixi but was struck by cannon and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: Ward took Cixi but was killed by cannon fire in the field.

sentences.zh: 陳公嶺不守，奉化复陷，郡城又警。

translations.literal: Chenggong Ridge could not be held; Fenghua fell again; the prefectural city was alarmed once more.
translations.idiomatic: Chenggong Ridge could not be held, Fenghua fell again, and the prefectural seat was once more threatened.

sentences.zh: 致諤乞餉於上海，令都司楊應龍募忠勇軍，紳士李諤招大嵐山義勇，又以廣勇潰散，慮為賊用，招之回，令洋將布興有、布良帶，守備張其光分統之。

translations.literal: Zhie begged funds from Shanghai, ordered Colonel Yang Yinglong to recruit the Zhongyong Army, gentry Li E to recruit Dalanshan volunteers; fearing the scattered Guang braves would serve rebels, he recalled them and had foreign officers Burgevine and Burgevine junior and Garrison Commander Zhang Qiguang command them separately.
translations.idiomatic: Zhie sought funds from Shanghai, had Colonel Yang Yinglong raise the Zhongyong Army and the gentryman Li E recruit Dalanshan volunteers; fearing the routed Guang braves would join the rebels, he recalled them and placed them under the foreign officers Burgevine and his nephew and Garrison Commander Zhang Qiguang.

sentences.zh: 部署甫定，賊由間道犯郡城，天雨陰霾，勒兵以待，伺賊懈出擊之，分兵兜剿，連捷於橫溪、石橋。

translations.literal: Dispositions had just been set when rebels came by a hidden path against the prefectural city; rain fell and the sky was dark; he held troops in readiness, watched for rebel slackness and struck, divided forces for encirclement, and won successive victories at Hengxi and Shiqiao.
translations.idiomatic: His dispositions were barely set when rebels came by a hidden route against the prefectural city; in rain and gloom he held his men ready, struck when the rebels slackened, sent detachments to cut them off, and won successive victories at Hengxi and Shiqiao.

sentences.zh: 進薄奉化，楊應龍率死士以梯登城，下之。

translations.literal: Advancing close to Fenghua, Yang Yinglong led dare-to-die men up ladders onto the wall and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing on Fenghua, Yang Yinglong led dare-to-die men up ladders onto the walls and took the city.

sentences.zh: 時致諤已實授寧紹台道。

translations.literal: By then Zhie had been formally appointed Ning-Shao-Tai intendant.
translations.idiomatic: By then Zhie had been formally appointed intendant of Ning-Shao-Tai Circuit.

sentences.zh: 奉化竄賊复勾結上虞賊分道犯慈谿、餘姚。

translations.literal: Fleeing rebels from Fenghua again joined Shangyu rebels to attack Cixi and Yuyao by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels who had fled Fenghua again joined forces with Shangyu rebels and struck Cixi and Yuyao by separate routes.

sentences.zh: 致諤以賊眾兵寡，分援則力弱，議直搗上虞，賊必還救，因出師漸遠，郡城餉事不能兼顧，乃請巡撫疏免前署道張景渠罪，責其專任兵事。

translations.literal: Zhie judged that rebels were many and troops few; dividing relief would weaken force; he proposed striking straight at Shangyu so rebels must return to rescue; as the army marched farther he could not also manage prefectural supplies; he asked the governor to memorialize pardoning former acting intendant Zhang Jingqu and charge him solely with military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhie reasoned that the rebels outnumbered his troops and that splitting his force would weaken it; he proposed striking directly at Shangyu so the rebels would have to turn back; as his army marched farther he could no longer manage supplies for the prefectural seat, so he asked the governor to memorialize a pardon for the former acting intendant Zhang Jingqu and put him in sole charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 連复上虞、嵊縣、新昌，增軍萬人，進規紹興。

translations.literal: He recovered in succession Shangyu, Sheng and Xinchang, increased the army by ten thousand, and advanced to plan recovery of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: He retook Shangyu, Sheng, and Xinchang in succession, raised his force by ten thousand men, and advanced against Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 二年，復之。

translations.literal: In the second year he recovered it.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he retook it.

sentences.zh: 進克蕭山，與大軍會於錢塘江，浙東以平。

translations.literal: He advanced and took Xiaoshan, joined the great army at the Qiantang River, and eastern Zhe was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced and took Xiaoshan, joined the main army at the Qiantang River, and eastern Zhejiang was pacified.

sentences.zh: 巡撫左宗棠奏減杭、嘉、湖三府漕賦，致諤上書言：「蠲賦惠政，減正額尤當革浮收，各縣情形各異。

translations.literal: Governor Zuo Zongtang memorialized to reduce grain transport taxes in Hang, Jia and Hu prefectures; Zhie wrote: "Tax remission is a benevolent policy; when reducing the regular quota one should especially abolish excess collections; each county's situation differs.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Zuo Zongtang memorialized to reduce grain-transport taxes in Hang, Jia, and Hu prefectures; Zhie wrote, "Tax relief is a benevolent measure, but when cutting the regular quota one must especially abolish excess collections, for each county's circumstances differ.
