sentences.zh: 當擇大者奏諮，餘並著為省例，以盡通變之宜。」

translations.literal: The major cases should be chosen for memorial and consultation; the rest should all be made provincial precedents to fulfill the need for flexible adaptation."
translations.idiomatic: The major cases should be memorialized for approval, and the rest set as provincial precedents so the policy can be adapted flexibly."

sentences.zh: 三年，以籌餉功，加按察使銜，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the third year for merit in raising funds he was given surveillance commissioner rank and granted peacock feathers.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, for his work in raising funds, he was given the rank of surveillance commissioner and granted peacock feathers.

sentences.zh: 先以衰老乞歸，未允，至是原品休致，卒於家。

translations.literal: Earlier he had begged to retire on grounds of age and was not granted; now he retired at his original rank and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He had earlier asked to retire on grounds of age and been refused; he now retired at his original rank and died at home.

sentences.zh: 劉郇膏，字松岩，河南太康人。

translations.literal: Liu Huangao, style name Songyan, was a native of Taikang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huangao, whose style was Songyan, came from Taikang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 道光二十七年進士，江蘇即用知縣。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination and was appointed magistrate for immediate use in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the twenty-seventh year of Daoguang and was appointed for immediate use as a magistrate in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，署婁縣，有政聲。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he acted as magistrate of Lou county and gained reputation for good administration.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng he served as acting magistrate of Lou county and earned a reputation for sound governance.

sentences.zh: 三年，粵匪陷江寧，揚州、鎮江相繼失守。

translations.literal: In the third year Cantonese bandits took Jiangning; Yangzhou and Zhenjiang fell in succession.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Cantonese rebels took Jiangning, and Yangzhou and Zhenjiang fell in turn.

sentences.zh: 會匪劉麗川倡亂踞上海，附近川沙、南匯、嘉定、寶山、青浦諸廳縣並陷。

translations.literal: Secret-society bandit Liu Lichuan raised rebellion and seized Shanghai; nearby Chuansha, Nanhui, Jiading, Baoshan, Qingpu and other sub-prefectures and counties all fell.
translations.idiomatic: The secret-society leader Liu Lichuan raised a revolt and seized Shanghai; nearby Chuansha, Nanhui, Jiading, Baoshan, Qingpu, and other districts fell as well.

sentences.zh: 巡撫吉爾杭阿檄郇膏隨營勦賊，郇膏率漕勇三百复嘉定，權知縣事，選丁壯嚴守望，稽保甲，籍遊民，民心大定。

translations.literal: Governor Ji'erhang'a ordered Huangao to follow the camp in suppressing bandits; Huangao led three hundred grain-transport braves to recover Jiading, acted as magistrate, selected strong men for strict watch, checked the baojia rolls, registered vagrants, and popular hearts were greatly settled.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Ji'erhang'a ordered Huangao to join the campaign against the rebels; Huangao led three hundred grain-transport braves to retake Jiading, took charge as magistrate, posted strong men on watch, checked the baojia registers, registered vagrants, and restored public confidence.

sentences.zh: 敘功，加同知銜，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Merit was entered; he was given sub-prefect rank and granted peacock feathers.
translations.idiomatic: His achievements were recorded; he was given sub-prefect rank and granted peacock feathers.

sentences.zh: 補青浦。

translations.literal: Appointed to Qingpu.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed to Qingpu.

sentences.zh: 八年，調上海。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was transferred to Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was transferred to Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 租界華洋雜處，數構釁，郇膏爭執是非，不為撓屈。

translations.literal: In the concession Chinese and foreigners lived mixed together and incidents arose repeatedly; Huangao argued right and wrong and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: In the foreign concession, where Chinese and foreigners lived side by side, disputes arose repeatedly; Huangao stood firm on what was right and would not be pushed aside.

sentences.zh: 有招工誘逼出洋者，親登舟搜獲，並追回已去者，民感之，洋人亦帖服。

translations.literal: When labor recruiters deceived and forced men overseas, he personally boarded ships to search and seize them and also brought back those already gone; the people were grateful and foreigners also submitted.
translations.idiomatic: When labor brokers deceived and coerced men into going overseas, he boarded the ships in person to seize them and brought back those already taken; the people were grateful and the foreigners submitted as well.

sentences.zh: 蘇、杭既陷，上海孤懸賊中，郇膏練民兵，四鄉設二十局，以資保衛。

translations.literal: After Suzhou and Hangzhou fell, Shanghai hung isolated amid rebels; Huangao trained militia and set up twenty stations in the four townships for defense.
translations.idiomatic: After Suzhou and Hangzhou fell, Shanghai stood isolated amid the rebels; Huangao trained militia and set up twenty defense stations across the surrounding townships.

sentences.zh: 賊首李秀成陷松江，進犯上海。

translations.literal: Rebel chief Li Xiucheng took Songjiang and advanced against Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel chief Li Xiucheng took Songjiang and advanced on Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 登陴堅守十餘日，賊不得逞而去。

translations.literal: He mounted the walls and held fast for more than ten days; the rebels could not prevail and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He manned the walls and held firm for more than ten days until the rebels withdrew without success.

sentences.zh: 時大吏萃居上海，或議他徙。

translations.literal: At the time high officials all gathered in Shanghai; some discussed moving elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: High officials were then gathered in Shanghai, and some talked of relocating.

sentences.zh: 郇膏曰：「滬城據海口，為餉源所自出，異日規復全省，必自此始。

translations.literal: Huangao said: "The Shanghai city sits on the sea mouth and is the source of army funds; when we plan one day to recover the whole province, we must begin here.
translations.idiomatic: Huangao said, "Shanghai sits on the sea route and is the source of army funds; when we one day plan to recover the whole province, we must begin here.

sentences.zh: 奈何舍而去之？」

translations.literal: How can we abandon it and leave?"
translations.idiomatic: How can we abandon it and walk away?"

sentences.zh: 十一年冬，賊复陷浦東諸廳縣，大吏檄郇膏往援，郇膏曰：「賊勢張甚，宜守不宜戰。」

translations.literal: In the winter of the eleventh year rebels again took the Pudong sub-prefectures and counties; high officials ordered Huangao to relieve them; Huangao said: "The rebel force is very strong; we should defend, not fight.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the eleventh year the rebels again took the Pudong districts; the high officials ordered Huangao to the relief; Huangao said, "The rebels are too strong—we should hold, not fight.

sentences.zh: 弗聽，率練勇、鄉團出戰，果敗，乃專議守。

translations.literal: They did not listen; he led militia and village braves out to battle and was indeed defeated; thereafter they discussed only defense.
translations.idiomatic: They would not listen; he led militia and village braves into battle and was defeated; after that the talk turned only to holding the city.

sentences.zh: 治行上聞，加道銜，以知府用。

translations.literal: His governance was reported upward; he was given circuit rank and used as prefect.
translations.idiomatic: His record of governance was reported to the court; he was given circuit rank and appointed prefect.

sentences.zh: 擢海防同知，超署按察使。

translations.literal: Promoted to coastal defense sub-prefect, he was extraordinarily appointed acting surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to coastal-defense sub-prefect, he was extraordinarily made acting surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 尋實授，命署布政使，異數也！

translations.literal: Soon formally appointed, he was ordered to act as administration commissioner—an exceptional favor!
translations.idiomatic: Soon formally appointed, he was ordered to serve as acting administration commissioner—an exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 李鴻章督師至，命總理營務，饋運無缺，兼協濟江寧大營，兩軍​​月餉二十萬，悉取給於上海。

translations.literal: When Li Hongzhang arrived to command the army he was ordered to manage camp affairs comprehensively; supplies were never lacking; he also assisted the Jiangning great camp; monthly pay of two hundred thousand for both armies all came from Shanghai.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Hongzhang arrived to take command he was put in charge of camp affairs; supplies never failed; he also supported the Jiangning headquarters; the two hundred thousand taels in monthly pay for both armies all came from Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 濬吳淞江以通運道，招集流亡，通商惠工，善後諸事，次第舉行。

translations.literal: He dredged the Wusong River to open transport routes, gathered displaced people, promoted trade and benefited crafts, and carried out recovery measures in succession.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged the Wusong River to open transport routes, gathered the displaced, promoted trade and industry, and carried out recovery measures one after another.

sentences.zh: 尋命護理巡撫，丁母憂。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to act as governor but went into mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to act as governor but entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 同治五年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tongzhi he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fifth year of Tongzhi.

sentences.zh: 贈右都御史，上海建專祠，祀蘇州名宦。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Right Censor-in-Chief; a special shrine was built in Shanghai and he was enshrined among Suzhou's eminent officials.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Right Censor-in-Chief; a special shrine was built in Shanghai and he was enshrined among Suzhou's eminent officials.

sentences.zh: 硃善張，字子弓，浙江平湖人。

translations.literal: Zhu Shanzhang, style name Zigong, was a native of Pinghu in Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shanzhang, whose style was Zigong, came from Pinghu in Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 諸生。

translations.literal: A licentiate.
translations.idiomatic: He was a licentiate.

sentences.zh: 授桃南通判，升里河同知。

translations.literal: Appointed sub-prefect of Taonan, promoted to sub-prefect of the Inner Canal.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed sub-prefect of Taonan and promoted to sub-prefect of the Inner Canal.

sentences.zh: 咸豐九年，擢淮徐揚海道。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Xianfeng he was promoted to Huai-Xu-Yang-Hai Circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Xianfeng he was promoted to intendant of Huai-Xu-Yang-Hai Circuit.

sentences.zh: 粵匪、捻匪時擾江北，奸民乘時蜂起。

translations.literal: Cantonese and Nian bandits repeatedly harassed the north of the river; bad elements rose like bees in season.
translations.idiomatic: Cantonese and Nian rebels repeatedly harassed the country north of the Yangtze, and ruffians rose everywhere to take advantage of the disorder.

sentences.zh: 善張常在行間，剿幅匪於海州、沭陽​​，殲其渠，賜花翎，加鹽運使銜。

translations.literal: Shanzhang was constantly in the ranks, suppressed coastal bandits at Haizhou and Shuyang, destroyed their chiefs, was granted peacock feathers and given salt commissioner rank.
translations.idiomatic: Shanzhang was constantly in the field, suppressed coastal bandits at Haizhou and Shuyang, destroyed their leaders, and was granted peacock feathers and the rank of salt commissioner.

sentences.zh: 捻首張隆據浮山，令水師伏臨淮焚其舟，又卻之小溪。

translations.literal: Nian chief Zhang Long held Fushan; he ordered the naval force to ambush at Linhuai and burn their boats, and also repelled them at Xiaoxi.
translations.idiomatic: Nian leader Zhang Long held Fushan; he had the naval force ambush them at Linhuai and burn their boats, and also drove them back at Xiaoxi.

sentences.zh: 粵匪陷天長，撲蔣壩，善张驰援，殪其酋，賜號庫木勒濟特依巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Cantonese bandits took Tianchang and struck Jiangba; Shanzhang rushed to relieve, killed their chief, and was granted the title Kumulejite Yibaturu.
translations.idiomatic: Cantonese rebels took Tianchang and struck Jiangba; Shanzhang rushed to the relief, killed their chief, and was granted the title Kumulejite Yibaturu.

sentences.zh: 善張方駐揚州，陳玉成來犯，攻城，發巨砲擊之，賊結堅壘為久困計。

translations.literal: Shanzhang was then stationed at Yangzhou when Chen Yucheng came to attack, besieged the city, fired great cannon at them; the rebels built strong forts planning a long siege.
translations.idiomatic: Shanzhang was at Yangzhou when Chen Yucheng attacked, besieged the city, and fired great cannon at the rebels, who built strong forts intending a long siege.

sentences.zh: 援師集，敗之七里店，追越儀徵以西，揚州獲安。

translations.literal: Relief armies gathered, defeated them at Qilidian, pursued beyond Yizheng to the west, and Yangzhou was secured.
translations.idiomatic: Relief forces gathered, defeated them at Qilidian, pursued them west of Yizheng, and Yangzhou was secured.

sentences.zh: 尋賊复麕至，連營至司徒廟。

translations.literal: Soon rebels gathered again in force and camped in succession as far as Situgong Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the rebels massed again and pitched camp after camp as far as Situgong Temple.

sentences.zh: 善張晝夜守陴，時出殺賊，賊卒不得逞，引去。

translations.literal: Shanzhang guarded the walls day and night, sallied out from time to time to kill rebels; the rebels in the end could not prevail and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Shanzhang held the walls day and night, sallied out repeatedly to strike the rebels, and in the end they withdrew without success.

sentences.zh: 十年，捻匪陷清江浦，率師克之，築圩寨為善後計。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Nian bandits took Qingjiangpu; he led troops to recover it and built stockaded villages as a recovery measure.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Nian rebels took Qingjiangpu; he led troops to retake it and built stockaded villages as a long-term measure.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，調徐州道，兼筦糧台，用堅壁清野法防捻匪。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was transferred to Xuzhou Circuit, also managed the grain bureau, and used the fortified-village and scorched-earth method against Nian bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he was transferred to Xuzhou Circuit, also managed the grain bureau, and used fortified villages and scorched-earth tactics against the Nian.

sentences.zh: 從僧格林沁攻孫甿老巢，破之棗溝。

translations.literal: He followed Senggelinqin in attacking Sun Meng's old nest and broke it at Zaogou.
translations.idiomatic: He served under Senggelinqin in the attack on Sun Meng's stronghold and broke it at Zaogou.

sentences.zh: 二年，苗沛霖叛，陷壽州，圍蒙城。

translations.literal: In the second year Miao Peilin rebelled, took Shouzhou and besieged Mengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year Miao Peilin rebelled, took Shouzhou, and besieged Mengcheng.

sentences.zh: 善張知蒙城餉絕，輸粟助之。

translations.literal: Shanzhang knew Mengcheng's supplies were cut off and sent grain to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Mengcheng's supplies were exhausted, Shanzhang sent grain to its relief.

sentences.zh: 苗沛霖伏誅，湖團之亂起。

translations.literal: Miao Peilin was executed in secret; the Lake Corps disturbance arose.
translations.idiomatic: After Miao Peilin was executed, the Lake Corps disturbances broke out.

sentences.zh: 湖團者，始議招流民開微山湖，自沛縣至魚台，戶數万，爭利亡命，遷跡其中。

translations.literal: The Lake Corps were first proposed to recruit displaced people to open Weishan Lake from Pei county to Yutai—tens of thousands of households, fighting for profit and fleeing the law, migrated and settled within.
translations.idiomatic: The Lake Corps were originally settlers recruited to open land around Weishan Lake from Pei county to Yutai—tens of thousands of households who fought over profits, fled the law, and made their homes there.

sentences.zh: 三年，新團匪殺掠沛縣劉民寨圩，善張會兵剿之，未竟，疽發背卒。

translations.literal: In the third year the New Corps bandits killed and plundered Liu Minzhai stockade in Pei county; Shanzhang joined troops to suppress them but before finishing died of a carbuncle on his back.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the New Corps bandits raided Liu Minzhai stockade in Pei county; Shanzhang joined the suppression but died of a back abscess before it was finished.

sentences.zh: 贈右都御史，賜卹。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Right Censor-in-Chief; condolence gifts were granted.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Right Censor-in-Chief and granted condolence gifts.

sentences.zh: 子之榛，以廕授官，補蘇州府總捕同知。

translations.literal: His son Zhizhen entered office by hereditary privilege and was appointed general pursuit sub-prefect of Suzhou prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhizhen entered office by hereditary privilege and was appointed general pursuit sub-prefect of the Suzhou prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歷以海運敘勞，晉秩道員。

translations.literal: Repeatedly merit was entered for sea transport and he was advanced to circuit intendant rank.
translations.idiomatic: His work on sea transport was repeatedly entered for merit, and he was raised to circuit intendant rank.

sentences.zh: 官江蘇凡四十年，筦釐務最久。

translations.literal: He served in Jiangsu for forty years in all, managing likin affairs the longest.
translations.idiomatic: He served in Jiangsu for forty years altogether, longest in charge of likin affairs.

sentences.zh: 精於綜覈，以剔除中飽為職志，地方利病，無不洞悉。

translations.literal: Skilled in comprehensive audit, he made eliminating middlemen's skim his vocation; local benefits and harms—none he did not thoroughly know.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled at auditing accounts, he made eliminating graft his life's work and knew every local problem inside out.

sentences.zh: 署督糧道。

translations.literal: Acting grain transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as acting grain transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 歷署按察使十二次、布政使二次，大吏倚之。

translations.literal: He acted as surveillance commissioner twelve times and administration commissioner twice; high officials relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: He served twelve times as acting surveillance commissioner and twice as acting administration commissioner, and the province's leaders relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 忌者眾，屢被彈劾，按治皆得白。

translations.literal: He had many enviers and was repeatedly impeached; investigations always cleared him.
translations.idiomatic: He had many enemies and was repeatedly impeached, but every investigation cleared him.

sentences.zh: 光緒二十五年，清釐田賦，歲增漕糧十五萬石、丁銀二​​十萬兩。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year of Guangxu he cleared land tax registers; yearly grain transport increased by 150,000 shi and poll tax silver by 200,000 taels.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year of Guangxu he cleared the land-tax registers, increasing annual grain transport by 150,000 shi and poll-tax silver by 200,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，海防戒嚴，省城獄囚謀變，之榛方署臬篆，出情實者駢誅之，事乃定。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year coastal defense was on alert; provincial capital prisoners plotted mutiny; Zhizhen was then acting surveillance commissioner; those found guilty in fact were executed in pairs and the matter was settled.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year, with coastal defenses on alert, prisoners in the provincial capital plotted a mutiny; Zhizhen was then acting surveillance commissioner; he executed the ringleaders in batches and the affair was settled.

sentences.zh: 宣統元年，授淮揚道，未任，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xuantong he was appointed Huai-Yang Circuit intendant but did not take office before he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xuantong he was appointed intendant of Huai-Yang Circuit but died before he could take up the post.

sentences.zh: 黃輔辰，字琴塢，貴州貴築人，原籍湖南醴陵。

translations.literal: Huang Fuchen, style name Qinwu, was a native of Guizhu in Guizhou, original domicile Liling in Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Fuchen, whose style was Qinwu, was registered in Guizhu in Guizhou but came from Liling in Hunan.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年進士，授吏部主事，累遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he passed the metropolitan examination, was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel, and was promoted repeatedly to director.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the fifteenth year of Daoguang, was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel, and rose repeatedly to director.

sentences.zh: 遇事侃侃持正論，屢忤上官，不少屈，時稱「硬黃」。

translations.literal: In affairs he spoke frankly and held upright views, repeatedly offended superiors and would not yield slightly; at the time he was called "Hard Huang."
translations.idiomatic: In office he spoke frankly and held to what he thought right, repeatedly offended his superiors and would not bend; people called him Hard Huang.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，以知府分山西。

translations.literal: Early in Xianfeng he was assigned as prefect to Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xianfeng reign he was posted to Shanxi as a prefect.

sentences.zh: 會貴州亂作，遽歸倡團練，修碉堡，積穀省城二萬餘石，撫清水江諸苗，平巴香亂，以功晉道員。

translations.literal: When rebellion broke out in Guizhou he hurried home to promote militia training, built blockhouses, stored more than twenty thousand shi of grain in the provincial capital, pacified the Miao along the Qingshui River, quelled the Baxiang disturbance, and for merit was advanced to circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion broke out in Guizhou he hurried home to organize militia, built blockhouses, stored more than twenty thousand shi of grain in the capital, pacified the Miao along the Qingshui River, quelled the Baxiang uprising, and was promoted to circuit intendant for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 尋赴山西，署冀寧道。

translations.literal: Soon he went to Shanxi and acted as Jining Circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went to Shanxi and served as acting intendant of Jining Circuit.

sentences.zh: 餉絀，議加釐捐，輔辰謂晉人皆賈於外，山多地瘠，非他行省比，不宜病民。

translations.literal: Army funds were short and likin surcharges were proposed; Fuchen said Shanxi people all traded outside the province, the mountains were many and the land lean—not comparable to other provinces—and it was unsuitable to burden the people.
translations.idiomatic: When army funds ran short and extra likin was proposed, Fuchen argued that Shanxi people traded abroad, the province was mountainous and poor, unlike other provinces, and the people should not be squeezed.

sentences.zh: 爭之不得，則請蠲苛細，取大宗，及不切民生日用者。

translations.literal: Unable to win the argument, he then asked to remit petty items, take only major categories, and exclude what did not touch the people's daily livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: When he could not prevail, he asked that petty items be remitted, only major categories retained, and everyday necessities left untouched.

sentences.zh: 戶部設寶泉分局於平定州，就鑄鐵錢。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue set up a Baoquan branch at Pingdingzhou to cast iron cash on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue set up a Baoquan branch at Pingdingzhou to cast iron cash locally.

sentences.zh: 滯不行，則令分銷諸郡縣，歲收息銀三萬解部。

translations.literal: When circulation lagged they ordered distribution through prefectures and counties, collecting thirty thousand taels interest yearly for remittance to the ministry.
translations.idiomatic: When the coins would not circulate, they ordered them distributed through the prefectures and counties, remitting thirty thousand taels in annual interest to the ministry.

sentences.zh: 輔辰謂：「京師用鐵錢以濟銅幣之乏，山西勿便也。

translations.literal: Fuchen said: "The capital uses iron cash to relieve shortage of copper coin; Shanxi should not follow suit.
translations.idiomatic: Fuchen said, "The capital uses iron cash to ease a shortage of copper coin; Shanxi should not do the same.

sentences.zh: 今行各縣，議令交納錢糧，以三萬之微利，妨數百萬之正供，利一而害百。

translations.literal: Now to circulate them in every county and propose payment of taxes and grain in them—to gain thirty thousand in petty profit while obstructing millions in regular revenue is one benefit and a hundred harms.
translations.idiomatic: To push them through every county and require tax payments in iron cash would gain thirty thousand taels in petty profit while obstructing millions in regular revenue—one small gain against a hundred harms.

sentences.zh: 即專行平定一州，日積日滯，其患滋大。」

translations.literal: Even if confined to Pingding prefecture alone, day by day accumulation and stagnation would make the harm grow greater.
translations.idiomatic: Even if limited to Pingding prefecture alone, the coins would pile up day by day and the harm would only grow.

sentences.zh: 議上，遂罷之。

translations.literal: The proposal was submitted upward and then abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on the matter and the scheme was dropped.

sentences.zh: 九年，調赴直隸軍營，察海口形勢，請以重兵扼北塘，當事迂其言，不用。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was transferred to the Zhili army camp, inspected the situation at the sea mouth, and requested heavy troops to hold Beitang; those in charge dismissed his words as impractical and did not use them.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was sent to the Zhili army camps, inspected the coastal situation, and urged that heavy troops hold Beitang; the authorities dismissed his advice and did not act on it.

sentences.zh: 尋乞假去。

translations.literal: Soon he requested leave and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He soon took leave and departed.

sentences.zh: 至四川，依總督駱秉章。

translations.literal: He reached Sichuan and attached himself to Governor Luo Bingzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Sichuan and served under Governor Luo Bingzhang.

sentences.zh: 陝西自回亂，地多荒蕪，巡撫劉蓉議興營田。

translations.literal: Since the Muslim rebellion in Shaanxi much land lay waste; Governor Liu Rong proposed establishing military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Muslim rebellion in Shaanxi much land had gone to waste; Governor Liu Rong proposed establishing military farm colonies.

sentences.zh: 輔辰書陳方略，採官私書為營田輯要三卷，大旨在用民而不用兵，與民興利，不與民牟利，蓉疏薦之。

translations.literal: Fuchen wrote setting forth strategy, gathered official and private writings into three volumes of Essentials for Military Colonies—the main idea being to use the people not soldiers, create benefit with the people not profit from them—and Rong memorialized recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: Fuchen laid out a plan in writing, compiled official and private sources into three volumes of Essentials for Military Colonies—the core idea being to rely on civilians rather than troops, to create benefit with the people rather than profit from them—and Rong memorialized recommending him.

sentences.zh: 五年，授陝西鳳邠鹽法道，任以西安、同州、鳳翔、延安、乾州、邠州、鄜州七屬營田事。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed Shaanxi Fengbin salt commissioner and charged with military colony affairs in the seven jurisdictions of Xi'an, Tongzhou, Fengxiang, Yan'an, Qianzhou, Binzhou and Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed salt commissioner of Fengbin in Shaanxi and put in charge of military farm colonies in the seven jurisdictions of Xi'an, Tongzhou, Fengxiang, Yan'an, Qianzhou, Binzhou, and Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 輔辰建議謂：「關中土曠人少，非招徠客民，事末由濟。

translations.literal: Fuchen proposed: "In Guanzhong land is broad and people few; unless guest settlers are recruited the undertaking cannot succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Fuchen proposed, "In Guanzhong land is abundant and people scarce; unless outside settlers are recruited the project cannot succeed.

sentences.zh: 然耕牛、耔種、農具、棚舍，官不能給，民不樂趨也。

translations.literal: Yet plow oxen, seed grain, farm tools and sheds—the government cannot supply them, and the people are not eager to come.
translations.idiomatic: Yet plow oxen, seed, tools, and shelters cannot all be supplied by the government, and the people will not come willingly.

sentences.zh: 莫若即以地畀之，薄收其租，畝二斗為差，六年後給券，使世其業。

translations.literal: Better to grant them the land directly, collect rent lightly at two dou per mu as standard, and after six years issue certificates so they may pass the occupation down through generations.
translations.idiomatic: Better to grant them the land outright, collect light rent at two dou per mu, and after six years issue certificates so they could pass the holding down through generations.

sentences.zh: 慮田無限制，賦無定則，吏得以意高下為民患，當先正經界，略如古井田法，量地百畝為區，編列次第，書賦額於券，視土肥瘠別等則上下授之。

translations.literal: Fearing land without limits and tax without fixed rule so clerks could raise or lower at will to the people's harm, boundaries should first be fixed, roughly like the ancient well-field system: measure land in hundred-mu districts, arrange in order, write tax quotas on certificates, and grant according to upper and lower grades depending on soil fertility.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing that without fixed boundaries and tax rates clerks would harass the people by arbitrary assessments, he proposed fixing boundaries first on something like the ancient well-field model: survey land in hundred-mu blocks, number them in order, write tax quotas on certificates, and assign grades according to soil fertility.

sentences.zh: 凡領墾者以先後為次，十區為甲，十甲為裡，置長焉。

translations.literal: All who received reclaimed land were ordered by priority; ten districts made a jia, ten jia a li, and heads were appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Reclaimers were ranked by priority; ten blocks formed a jia, ten jia a li, each with a headman.

sentences.zh: 里長總十甲租課，歲輸之官，凡移徙更替事皆責之。

translations.literal: The li head collected rent from ten jia and remitted yearly to the government; all matters of moving, replacing and turnover were his responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: The li head collected rent from ten jia and paid it yearly to the government, and was responsible for all moves, replacements, and turnover.

sentences.zh: 別授田六畝，俾食其入，為庶人在官者之祿，而官總其成。」

translations.literal: Separately six mu were granted so they could live on its yield as salary for commoners in office, while the government oversaw the whole.
translations.idiomatic: Six mu were set aside separately so local officers could live on the yield as salary, while the government retained overall control.

sentences.zh: 令下，民皆便之。

translations.literal: When the order was issued the people all found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: When the order went out the people welcomed it.

sentences.zh: 复定考課舉劾法，策奉行不力者。

translations.literal: He also fixed examination and impeachment methods and urged punishment of those who carried out the policy poorly.
translations.idiomatic: He also set examination and impeachment rules and pressed action against officials who implemented the policy poorly.

sentences.zh: 期年，凡墾田十八萬餘畝。

translations.literal: Within a year more than 180,000 mu were reclaimed in all.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year more than 180,000 mu were brought under cultivation.

sentences.zh: 時軍事急，賴所入租麥以餉之。

translations.literal: At the time military affairs were urgent and army provisions relied on the rent grain and wheat received.
translations.idiomatic: Military needs were urgent at the time, and army provisions relied on the rent grain and wheat the colonies produced.

sentences.zh: 又撥產給書院、義學、養濟院、育嬰堂、種痘局及灞岸堤工、渠工，諸廢皆舉。

translations.literal: He also allocated estates to academies, charity schools, poorhouses, orphanages, vaccination bureaus, and Ba River embankment and canal works; all abandoned projects were undertaken.
translations.idiomatic: He also allocated land to academies, charity schools, poorhouses, orphanages, vaccination offices, and Ba River embankment and canal works, reviving one abandoned project after another.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，祀名宦。

translations.literal: Soon he died and was enshrined among eminent officials.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died and was enshrined in the local hall of eminent officials.

sentences.zh: 子彭年，字子壽。

translations.literal: His son Pengnian, style name Zishou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pengnian, whose style was Zishou.

sentences.zh: 舉道光二十五年會試，逾兩年，改庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: He passed the metropolitan examination in the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang; after more than two years he was changed to Hanlin bachelor and appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the metropolitan examination in the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang; two years later he became a Hanlin bachelor and was appointed a compiler.

sentences.zh: 咸豐初，隨父在籍治團練，後入駱秉章四川戎幕，數有贊畫功，不受保薦。

translations.literal: Early in Xianfeng he followed his father in native place to manage militia; later he entered Luo Bingzhang's Sichuan military secretariat, repeatedly contributed planning merit, and would not accept recommendation.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xianfeng he helped his father organize militia at home; later he joined Luo Bingzhang's military staff in Sichuan, contributed repeatedly to planning, and refused recommendations for office.

sentences.zh: 同治初，劉蓉延主關中書院。

translations.literal: Early in Tongzhi Liu Rong invited him to head the Guanzhong Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tongzhi Liu Rong invited him to direct the Guanzhong Academy.

sentences.zh: 久之，李鴻章聘修畿輔通志，兼主蓮池書院。

translations.literal: After a long while Li Hongzhang engaged him to compile the Jifu gazetteer and also to head the Lianchi Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Hongzhang engaged him to compile the Jifu gazetteer and also to head the Lianchi Academy.

sentences.zh: 當光緒中，法、俄邊事迭起，侍從近臣多慷慨建言，彭年雖不在朝，負時望，中外大臣密薦之。

translations.literal: During Guangxu border troubles with France and Russia arose in succession; attendant close ministers spoke boldly with many proposals; Pengnian though not at court bore contemporary esteem and ministers at home and abroad secretly recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: During the Guangxu era border troubles with France and Russia arose one after another; courtiers spoke out boldly, and though Pengnian was not in office he enjoyed wide esteem and was quietly recommended by ministers at home and abroad.

sentences.zh: 八年，擢授湖北襄鄖荊道，遷按察使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was promoted and appointed Xiang-Yun-Jing Circuit of Hubei, then transferred to surveillance commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was promoted to Xiang-Yun-Jing Circuit in Hubei and then made surveillance commissioner.

sentences.zh: 屏餽遺，禁胥吏需索，年餘，結京控案四十餘起，平反大獄十數。

translations.literal: He rejected gifts, forbade clerks and runners to demand fees; in more than a year he concluded more than forty capital-appeal cases and reversed more than ten major wrongful convictions.
translations.idiomatic: He refused gifts, forbade clerks and runners to extort fees, and within a year closed more than forty capital appeals and reversed more than ten major wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 調陝西，署布政使。

translations.literal: Transferred to Shaanxi, he acted as administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Transferred to Shaanxi, he served as acting administration commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遷江蘇布政使。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was moved to Jiangsu administration commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was transferred to administration commissioner of Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 連歲水旱，米踴貴，屬縣請加漕折，巡撫欲許之，彭年謂：「定例漕糧一石，隨徵水腳錢一千，所費僅數百，獨不可以有餘補不足耶？

translations.literal: Years of flood and drought in succession made rice soar in price; subordinate counties asked to increase grain transport surcharges; the governor wished to grant it; Pengnian said: "By regulation one shi of transport grain carries one thousand cash transport fee, costing only several hundred—can surplus not cover shortage?
translations.idiomatic: After successive floods and droughts rice prices soared; subordinate counties asked to raise grain-transport surcharges and the governor was inclined to agree; Pengnian said, "By regulation each shi of transport grain carries a transport fee of one thousand cash, costing only a few hundred—cannot surplus cover shortage?

sentences.zh: 今增漕折，民間多出二十萬緡，與國計無關，盡歸中飽。」

translations.literal: To increase transport surcharges now would make the people pay out an extra two hundred thousand strings, unrelated to state revenue, all going to middlemen's skim."
translations.idiomatic: Raising the surcharge now would make the people pay an extra two hundred thousand strings, none of it reaching state revenue and all of it going to graft."

sentences.zh: 持不可。

translations.literal: He held firm that it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: He held firm against it.

sentences.zh: 十五年，護理巡撫，請以賑餘三十萬緡濬吳淞江、白茆河、蘊藻浜，工未及舉，十六年，調湖北布政使，總督張之洞尤倚重之。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he acted as governor and requested three hundred thousand strings of relief surplus to dredge the Wusong River, Ba-mao River and Yunzao Creek; work had not yet begun when in the sixteenth year he was transferred to Hubei administration commissioner; Governor-General Zhang Zhidong especially relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he acted as governor and proposed using three hundred thousand strings of relief surplus to dredge the Wusong River, Ba-mao River, and Yunzao Creek; the work had not yet begun when in the sixteenth year he was transferred to administration commissioner of Hubei, where Governor-General Zhang Zhidong relied on him heavily.

sentences.zh: 然守正不阿，遇庫款出入，龂龂以爭，雖忤其意，勿顧也。

translations.literal: Yet he upheld rectitude without bending; whenever treasury funds went in or out he argued tooth and nail, even against the other's wishes, without regard.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he stood on principle without bending; on treasury receipts and disbursements he argued fiercely, even against Zhang's wishes, without flinching.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after.

sentences.zh: 彭年廉明剛毅，博學多通。

translations.literal: Pengnian was incorrupt, clear, firm and resolute, learned and broadly accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: Pengnian was incorruptible, resolute, learned, and widely accomplished.

sentences.zh: 所至，以陶成士類為國儲才為己任。

translations.literal: Wherever he went he took molding scholars and storing talent for the state as his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he served he made it his task to cultivate scholars and build up talent for the state.

sentences.zh: 主講蓮池及在吳時設學古堂，成就尤眾。

translations.literal: Heading the Lianchi Academy and establishing the Xuegu Hall while in Wu, his accomplished disciples were especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: As head of the Lianchi Academy and founder of the Xuegu Hall in Jiangsu, he trained an especially large number of accomplished disciples.

sentences.zh: 著有陶樓詩文集、三省邊防考略、金沙江考略、歷代關隘津梁考存、銅運考略。

translations.literal: He authored Collected Poems and Prose of Taolou, Brief Study of Border Defense in the Three Provinces, Brief Study of the Jinsha River, Preserved Studies of Passes and Ferries through the Ages, and Brief Study of Copper Transport.
translations.idiomatic: His works include Collected Poems and Prose of Taolou, Brief Study of Border Defense in the Three Provinces, Brief Study of the Jinsha River, Preserved Studies of Passes and Ferries through the Ages, and Brief Study of Copper Transport.

sentences.zh: 子國瑾，光緒二年進士，官編修。

translations.literal: His son Guojin, jinshi in the second year of Guangxu, served as compiler.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guojin, a jinshi in the second year of Guangxu, served as a compiler.

sentences.zh: 嗜學能文，甚有時譽。

translations.literal: Fond of learning and skilled in writing, he enjoyed great contemporary reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Devoted to learning and skilled in writing, he enjoyed a strong contemporary reputation.

sentences.zh: 父喪，以毀卒。

translations.literal: On his father's death he died from grief-induced injury.
translations.idiomatic: He died from grief and fasting after his father's death.

sentences.zh: 論曰：軍興以來，監司賢者，保障一方，其功與疆吏等。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Since the war began, worthy surveillance and circuit commissioners who secured a region—their merit equals that of frontier governors.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Since the war began, able surveillance and circuit commissioners who secured a region have earned merit equal to that of frontier governors.

sentences.zh: 軍政財政，各行省多有專任之人。

translations.literal: Military affairs and finance—in each province there were often persons with specialized duties.
translations.idiomatic: For military affairs and finance, each province often had officials with specialized responsibilities.

sentences.zh: 沈棣輝平廣匪，余炳燾守懷慶，其最著也。

translations.literal: Shen Dihui pacified Guang bandits and Yu Bingtao held Huaqing—the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Dihui pacified the Guang rebels and Yu Bingtao held Huaqing—the most celebrated cases.

sentences.zh: 鄧仁堃殫心籌防，不盡見用。

translations.literal: Deng Renkun exhausted his heart in planning defense but was not fully employed.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Renkun gave his all to planning defense but was not fully used.

sentences.zh: 硃孫貽提倡團練，振興人材，實為湘軍肇基。

translations.literal: Zhu Sunyi promoted militia training and revived talent—he truly laid the foundation of the Xiang Army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Sunyi promoted militia training and revived talent—he truly laid the foundations of the Xiang Army.

sentences.zh: 劉郇膏主守上海以待援軍。

translations.literal: Liu Huangao insisted on holding Shanghai to await relief armies.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Huangao insisted on holding Shanghai until relief armies could arrive.

sentences.zh: 皆以一縣令有裨大局。

translations.literal: All were county magistrates who benefited the larger situation.
translations.idiomatic: All were county magistrates who materially helped the larger cause.

sentences.zh: 史致諤用外兵定寧波，硃善張保障淮、揚，功皆可紀。

translations.literal: Shi Zhie used foreign troops to settle Ningbo; Zhu Shanzhang secured Huai and Yang—their merits can all be recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhie used foreign troops to recover Ningbo; Zhu Shanzhang secured the Huai and Yang regions—each left achievements worth recording.

sentences.zh: 栗耀筦湖北稅釐，黃輔辰興陝西營田，並為兵食根本。

translations.literal: Li Yao managed Hubei likin taxation and Huang Fuchen revived Shaanxi military colonies—both were foundations of army provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yao managed Hubei likin and Huang Fuchen revived Shaanxi military farm colonies—both underpinned the army's food supply.

sentences.zh: 黃彭年名父之子，久負時望，晚達未盡其用，時論惜之。

translations.literal: Huang Pengnian, son of a famous father, long bore contemporary esteem; achieving office late he did not fully use his talents, and opinion at the time regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Pengnian, son of a famous father, had long enjoyed public esteem; he rose late and never fully used his talents, to the regret of his contemporaries.
